job.title: Grid Operations Engineer
job.description:
Are you an experienced Electrical Engineer or Electrical Technician with wind turbine experience looking to take the next step in your career within the renewable energy sector?

Our client is seeking a Grid Operations Engineer to join their team in Kerry. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced wind energy professional to develop their expertise across MV/HV electrical systems, grid operations, switching operations and SCADA, with a clear pathway towards becoming a Switching Control Engineer for Ireland and the UK.

What you will be doing:

  • Authorising, supervising and carrying out MV/HV switching operations.
  • Supporting compliance with Irish legislation and procedures relating to HV electrical works.
  • Coordinating materials and labour for repairs and maintenance of MV/HV equipment.
  • Providing first-level technical support for SCADA monitoring and fault resolution.
  • Supporting SCADA installations during new projects and site refits.
  • Assisting technicians with fault finding, testing, breakdowns and technical issues on site.
  • Ensuring MV/HV and associated LV equipment is inspected and maintained in line with legislation and company procedures.
  • Liaising with site owners, operators, technicians and customers as required.
  • Preparing and maintaining technical documentation, reports and records.
  • Supporting technical and software updates across operational systems.
  • Following training and supervised experience, progressing into Switching Control Engineer responsibilities for Ireland and the UK, covering existing sites and first energisations.
  • Participating in a weekend on-call rota as required.
  • Travelling nationwide for training and technical support, with occasional international travel for training and workshops.

What we are looking for:

  • Electrical Trade Qualification or Electrical Engineering Degree is essential.
  • Minimum 4 years' experience within the wind turbine industry is essential.
  • Experience with SCADA monitoring and fault resolution is highly advantageous.
  • Strong knowledge of electrical systems, with MV/HV experience highly desirable.
  • Excellent fault-finding and problem-solving ability.
  • Strong IT skills and the ability to work with technical software and databases.
  • Excellent communication and organisational skills.
  • Ability to prepare clear technical reports and documentation.
  • Ability to work independently and manage workload effectively.
  • Flexible approach to work, including participation in weekend on-call duties.
  • Willingness to travel nationwide and internationally when required.
  • Commitment to progressing towards Authorised Engineer (AE) status within 6 months where required.

What is on offer:

  • Competitive salary based on experience.
  • Company pension.
  • Health & Dental Insurance.
  • Life Assurance.
  • 22 days annual leave, increasing to 30 days with length of service.
  • Paid Maternity and Paternity Leave.
  • Hybrid working model.
  • Training and ongoing professional development.
  • Excellent career progression opportunities.

If you are an experienced Electrical Engineer / Electrical Technician with 4+ years' wind turbine experience and are looking for an opportunity to progress into a specialist Grid Operations / Switching Control position, apply today with your CV.

job.title: Children & Youth Support Worker
job.description:
FRS Recruitment in Partnership with Aoibhneas

Role: Children & Youth Support Workers

Posts: Full-Time - Permanent - 39 Hours

Salary: €40,851 per annum

Reports to: Direct line Manager

Location: North Dublin Based

FRS Recruitment, in partnership with Aoibhneas, are seeking Children & Youth Support Workers to provide support and structured services to young people residing and engaged through Aoibhneas services.

The role is responsible for promoting and maintaining the safety and well-being of all children and young people accessing services, while also representing and upholding the values, ethos, and mission of Aoibhneas in all aspects of the work. Through this role, the successful candidate will enable children and young people to remain safe and supported within their own homes and communities, encouraging participation in children and youth activities.

Key Areas of Responsibility: Client Services & Administration

Including, but not limited to:

  • To make an initial assessment of a child’s and youth’s support needs and refer children and youth in need of a more in-depth assessment to the relevant agency in conjunction with the Social Care Leader and and other designated persons.
  • Maintain accurate and up to date records of all case files.
  • To work as part of the Social Care team, liaising with other staff and departments in relation to services and supports for children/families.
  • To develop and implement suitable programmes to meet the needs of the children and youth in refuge and community services.
  • To provide advice, information and support to non-residents by telephone and in person.
  • Ensure standards are maintained and adhered to inline with policy, procedure and legislation.

Essential Requirements:

  • Third Level Qualification at degree level in child care, childhood and youth development, social science, social care or related field.
  • A minimum of 3 years relevant work experience working in a social care setting with children/youth.
  • Experience of key-working clients or individual case-work.
  • Excellent knowledge and understanding of domestic violence and issues affecting women and children experiencing domestic violence.
  • Understanding and working knowledge of Children’s First Legislation/ Child Care Act.
  • Excellent facilitation, training and communication skills.

Desirable Criteria:

  • Flexibility/Adaptability
  • Experience of inter-agency working
  • Full driving License

Employer Benefits

  • Employer Pension Contribution of 5%.
  • Annual leave 22 days inclusive of 2 well-being days with incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision and Employee Assistance Programme.

All offers of employment with Aoibhneas are subject to Garda Vetting, satisfactory reference checks and verification of legal eligibility to work in Ireland. Aoibhneas is an equal opportunities employer. A Panel may be formed out of this recruitment process.

Contact: If you are interested in this opportunity please contact Chloe O Brien, Senior Recruitment Consultant, Tel: M: +353(0)86 1076802 for more information.

You will have responsibility and autonomy for scheduling maintenance for multiple Dairy farms. Our client is one of the largest vertically integrated dairy companies in the Middle East, managing over 195,000 dairy cows across seven modern dairy farms.

The FMM will work closely with farm workshop staff and demonstrate areas of improvement that can reduce costs / improve performance and reduce downtime on equipment. This will be a hands-on role where you will work with a multicultural workforce with a varying degree of ability.

The FMM will work side by side with the workshop team and transfer knowledge to them and help to improve their skills & ensure that the farm staff always keep updated service records.

Please note the ideal candidate for this role will be proficient in reading electrical and hydraulic drawings as you will be the contact for all mechanics when a breakdown arises.

Job overview

To plan and organize assigned farm mechanical maintenance staff so that the broad range of agricultural, industrial and animal feeding machinery and equipment is serviced, maintained and operated in accordance with company procedure. Train staff to ensure that competent and sufficient numbers of maintenance staff are available for the assigned farm sites.

Duties to include

  • To ensure that all maintenance staff are organised, trained and carry out all maintenance in accordance with all company Maintenance and Safety procedures for all farm agricultural, industrial and feeding machinery and equipment.
  • To ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out in a safe manner and in accordance with company policy and standards.
  • To ensure all workshop buildings and surrounding areas, tools, lifting equipment and electrical equipment are in a clean and safe working condition.
  • To minimise the level of unplanned stoppages of machinery and reduce production losses due to machinery or equipment downtime.
  • To oversee routine and preventative maintenance of all agricultural, industrial and feeding machinery and equipment within the Division.
  • To monitor and assess the performance of all maintenance staff in conjunction with the Farming and Maintenance Manager and recommend training as require.
  • Liaise with suppliers to arrange warranty repairs.
  • Report issues that affect the reliability and running costs of equipment.
  • Arrange OEM training and access to required manuals for workshop staff.
  • Update company manuals that are used for maintaining and servicing machinery. Ensure that workshop staff are always following company manuals for servicing.
  • Identify parts that should be kept in the workshop central store that are necessary to keep equipment running. Ensure that the workshop store does not carry obsolete stock.
  • Navigate different manufacturers parts manuals / systems.
  • Arrange quotations from suppliers for the repair of equipment.

Core competencies

  • Excellent communicator with good influencing and person management skills.
  • A sound knowledge of troubleshooting and diagnostic fault finding.
  • A sound experience with all types of agricultural and mechanical machinery.
  • High degree of confidence and or decision-making capability.
  • Focused under pressure, self-motivated, assertive, confident, fair, and open-minded.
  • Strong IT skills

Candidate profile

  • 5 years year’s + experience in a workshop or service centre environment
  • Experience in managing a large-scale maintenance.
  • Experience with maintenance of large scale agricultural and industrial equipment, and petrol and diesel engine Vehicles
  • Fully operational in the use of structured maintenance systems with a particular emphasis on a planned approach to preventive maintenance and recording and analysing data

What We Need From You

  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.

Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity to join one of the Midlands' most respected food manufacturers. A competitive salary, pension, and bonus package is on offer, along with the chance to work in a modern, state-of-the-art facility.

The company is recognised for its investment in people, technology, and continuous improvement, providing excellent opportunities for both personal and professional development. You'll be joining a progressive, fast-paced Irish success story where your ideas and contributions will be valued.

job.title: Financial Analyst & Commercial Modelling Specialist
job.description:
We are seeking a highly analytical and commercially minded Financial Analyst & Commercial Modelling Specialist due to business growth. Reporting to the Business Intelligence Manager, you will play a key role in supporting business growth through the development of financial models, commercial pricing solutions, tender submissions, and strategic business cases. Working closely with Commercial, Operations, HR, and Finance teams, you will ensure that pricing proposals are commercially competitive, financially robust, and aligned with organisational objectives.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys solving complex commercial challenges, and wants to make a tangible impact on business success.

A predominantly remote role with some days in the initial weeks working from a Tipperary office.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Modelling & Analysis

  • Develop, maintain, and enhance detailed financial models to support bids, tenders, business cases, and strategic projects.
  • Conduct financial forecasting, scenario planning, and sensitivity analysis to assess commercial opportunities and risks.
  • Ensure the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of all financial modelling outputs.
  • Analyse operational and financial performance data to support strategic decision-making.

Tender Pricing & Commercial Bid Support

  • Collaborate with operational and commercial stakeholders to gather cost, resource, and pricing assumptions.
  • Develop robust pricing models that balance competitiveness, profitability, and risk.
  • Support the preparation, review, and submission of tender responses and commercial proposals.
  • Evaluate contract opportunities and renewal pricing strategies.

Commercial Insight & Profitability Analysis

  • Assess customer, contract, and service-line profitability to identify opportunities for margin improvement and cost optimisation.
  • Provide recommendations that support sustainable business growth and commercial performance.
  • Monitor financial performance against targets and identify areas for improvement.

Forecasting & Business Planning

  • Support budgeting, forecasting, and long-term planning activities through detailed financial analysis.
  • Identify financial risks and opportunities that may impact business performance.
  • Provide insights that support resource allocation and investment decisions.

Stakeholder Engagement & Decision Support

  • Partner with stakeholders across Commercial, Operations, HR, and Finance functions.
  • Present financial findings, assumptions, and recommendations to a variety of audiences.
  • Translate complex financial data into clear and commercially relevant insights.

Governance & Continuous Improvement

  • Ensure compliance with internal governance, approval processes, and financial controls.
  • Maintain clear documentation and audit trails for pricing models and commercial assumptions.
  • Contribute to the ongoing enhancement of modelling methodologies, pricing frameworks, and commercial processes.

Essential Requirements

  • QQI Level 8 Honours Degree (or equivalent) in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years' experience in financial analysis, commercial finance, bid pricing, tender support, or financial modelling.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including financial modelling, forecasting, scenario analysis, and dashboard development.
  • Strong understanding of financial statements, budgeting, forecasting, and profitability analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex financial data into meaningful commercial insights and recommendations.
  • Strong commercial acumen with an understanding of pricing strategies and contract profitability.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a dynamic environment.
  • Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail.

Desirable Qualifications & Experience

  • Professional finance qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA or equivalent), or currently working towards qualification.
  • Experience supporting public or private sector tenders and procurement processes.
  • Experience using Power BI, SQL, ERP systems, or financial planning and analysis tools.
  • Experience within a contract-based, healthcare, facilities management, logistics, outsourced services, or related commercial environment.
  • Knowledge of pricing methodologies, contract costing, and commercial risk assessment.

Why Join Us?

  • Be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking organisation.
  • Play a key role in shaping commercial strategy and supporting business growth.
  • Work on high-impact projects and strategic business opportunities.
  • Opportunities for professional development and career progression.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.

Apply Today

If you are passionate about financial analysis, commercial strategy, and delivering insights that drive performance, we would love to hear from you. Apply today with an updated copy of your CV to Ciara Lawler for immediate consideration.

job.title: Case Worker
job.description:
Caseworker required to work in our Carlow Office

Monday-Friday 09:00-05:00(on-site)
We are looking for candidates with strong customer service and administration experience.


You will need to drive as you will have to travel for this role- you must have own car and full licence
ABOUT TURAS NUA
IPNES supports people who are over 12 months unemployed or employed part-time on low earnings, by providing intensive, targeted and personalised employment support services. The IPNES contract is delivered by Turas Nua, the Irish employability services provider. Turas Nua is wholly owned by FRS Network, an Irish cooperative social enterprise, which has been delivering services to Irish communities since 1980.


PURPOSE OF ROLE
As a caseworker, you will work with clients referred by the Department of Social Protection to IPNES. You will manage a caseload of clients, coordinating our internal support specialists and external organisations to provide a personalised, planned support service to each client, to help them gain sustainable employment. You will also provide each client with one-to-one advice and support to guide their progress towards employment.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop and manage a robust case management plan for each client, working towards sustainable, full-time employment.
  • use our industry-leading assessment technology to identify the client’s goals, ambitions, and barriers to employment. Use the output from the assessment to inform a structured personal progression plan, agreed with the client.
  • Recognise hidden motivations and conflict when assessing clients’ job-readiness, in order to address these with appropriate support and interventions.
  • Provide coaching and mentoring to clients, including providing intensive job search support when the client is job ready.
  • Identify, structure, and recommend training solutions in consultation with in-house tutors, to meet the specific learning and training needs of clients.
  • Fast-track job-ready clients for immediate job interviews brokered by our Employer Services consultants.
  • Maintain strong knowledge of the local labour market.
  • Organise a daily schedule that includes face-to-face meetings, phone calls, online meetings, and email correspondence with clients and other service providers.
  • Work closely with local and national specialist services (e.g., training, literacy, housing, health) to assist the client in their journey towards employment.
  • Present and facilitate workshops and group-learning presentations to clients weekly.
  • Achieve daily and monthly contractual key performance indicator (KPI) targets, managing a caseload of clients; for example, time-bound contacts, assessments, and support activities.
  • Provide guidance and support for more job-ready clients during their initial weeks of employment, helping them to successfully transition to sustainable employment.
  • Ensure that client interactions are recorded accurately on the CRM system.
  • Ensure data protection regulations are fully adhered to.


ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Leaving Certificate or equivalent.
  • Minimum of three years’ experience of working in a customer focused, target driven environment.
  • Strong IT skills/experience in the use of Microsoft office and CRM systems. Must be comfortable with all aspects of remote working technology.
  • Excellent administrative skills – fast & accurate data entry skills.
  • The ability to build rapport and work effectively with a diverse range of individuals both in person and over the phone.
  • Experience in delivering presentations in a group setting or public speaking.
  • Strong prioritisation and time management skills.
  • Fluent written and spoken English.

Recruiter:Joyce Coffey

job.title: Administrator and Care Coordinator Support
job.description:
Administrator and Care Coordinator Support

Purpose of role

To conduct effective coordination of Care Assistants to ensure that customers receive excellent quality care and support to keep them safe and comfortable in their own homes. A supportive and calm manner together with excellent organisational and communication skills are vital to excel in this role.

Key responsibility

Ensure that Care Assistants are appropriately rostered and allocated to customers so that care is delivered on time, safely and in line with customers wishes (as agreed in their care and support plan), and aligns with the agreed availability of Care Assistants. To strive to achieve optimised scheduling that meets the needs of both customers and carers.

Duties

  • Liaise with the Lead Coordinator and / or Registered Manager to ensure the right number of Care Assistants, with the right skills mixes, are recruited to meet the needs of the business. Arrange cover for Care Assistant sickness, absenteeism or holidays.
  • Accept, allocate and process new customer referrals for care and support promptly and effectively.
  • Process changes to customers’ required care and support needs.
  • Ensure there is sufficient cover to deliver care and support to all customers on time and in alignment with their personal care plans.
  • Monitor the restoring of Care Assistants to maximise efficiency whilst supporting them to maintain an appropriate work/ life balance.
  • Schedule Care Assistants to provide care and support to customers. Work with other members of the Care team to appropriately match Care Assistants to customers taking account of:
  1. Care Assistant skills, experience and availability to safely deliver the care and support plan;
  2. the customer’s preferences and care needs; and
  3. travel arrangements, routes and working patterns to make efficient use of Care Assistant time whilst meeting the needs of customers.
  • Make required adjustments to rotas as required to provide cover for emergency situations, to cover staff holiday or sickness, etc.
  • Distribute staff rotas at agreed intervals.
  • If required, take part in the out of hours emergency on-call rota. This will only be required after the post holder has received full training and has been assessed as competent to provide appropriate guidance and advice in emergency situations.
  • Work with the office team to maintain up to date electronic and hand written records. Use systems to record and monitor mileage and travel distances. Make sure that accidents and incidents are recorded, reported and acted upon.
  • Keep all information about customers and their families secure and confidential.
  • Carry out general office duties. Prepare reports as required as required by the Registered Manager.
  • Talk to customers and their chosen representatives about their care and support, taking account of different communication needs and levels of understanding.
  • Work with the team and other health and social care professionals to deliver high quality homecare services and to make improvements where necessary.
  • Work flexibly as part of the team and apply organisation policies and procedures at all times.

This list is not exhaustive and additional duties may be required.

Essential criteria

  • Kind and Caring – compassionate towards others who need support.
  • Professional and Respected - excellent time keeper, reliable and understanding of professional boundaries.
  • Dedicated to non-discriminatory care practice. This means respecting people suffering from a range of medical conditions with different backgrounds and beliefs to your own.
  • Innovative – strong problem-solver, who thinks outside of the box to identify solutions and opportunities.
  • Supportive – a team player and fantastic communicator, with good emotional intelligence.
  • Fun and Passionate – understand that home care can bring joy and happiness to a customers’ day, and strive to achieve this.

Knowledge and skills

  • Good understanding of the needs of people who need care and support.
  • Excellent organisational skills- proven ability to plan and organise workloads effectively so that customers receive the services they expect and are safe.
  • Ability to maintain clear and accurate written records and follow statutory reporting procedures.
  • Understanding of what confidentiality means in relation to home care services and why this is important.
  • Good administrative and IT skills. High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and build positive working relationships with customers, their families, staff and other health and social care professionals. Good telephone manner and interpersonal skills.
  • Knowledge of what confidentiality means in relation to home care services and why this is important.
  • Good geographical knowledge of the local area (roads / routes / traffic levels).
  • Ability to think clearly when under pressure. Comfortable using own initiative to solve problems or as part of a team especially in an emergency.
  • Ability and willingness to follow company’s policies, procedures and instructions

If you would like to work in an industry where you can make an impact on lives make sure to apply below.

INDFRS1

With operations across the UK, Northern Ireland and Turkey, they have built a strong reputation for technical expertise, quality and innovation.

📍 Co. Meath — commutable from Kells, Navan, Nobber, Kingscourt, Bailieborough, Virginia, Athboy and surrounding areas.

The Role

This is a hands-on, site-based position offering the opportunity to take ownership across both Quality and HSE, working closely with production and operational teams.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Supporting and maintaining the site QMS and HSE systems
  • Conducting quality, hygiene and safety inspections/audits
  • Managing product traceability, sampling, testing and positive release
  • Investigating non-conformances, incidents and customer complaints
  • Supporting HACCP, internal and external audits

job.title: Senior Occupational Therapist
job.description:
SENIOR OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST

Location: Westmeath
Permanent | Full-Time
Private Hospital Setting

I’m currently recruiting for a Senior Occupational Therapist to join a well-established private hospital in Westmeath.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced OT looking to join a supportive multidisciplinary team where you’ll have the opportunity to work across rehabilitation, functional assessment and discharge planning, while continuing to develop your clinical skills.

The Role

As a Senior Occupational Therapist, you’ll manage a varied caseload and provide high-quality, patient-centred Occupational Therapy from assessment through to intervention and discharge.

Your role will include:

• Completing comprehensive Occupational Therapy and functional assessments.

• Assessing patients’ ability to manage activities of daily living and identifying barriers to independence.

• Developing individualised treatment and rehabilitation plans based on patients’ goals and clinical needs.

• Supporting patients to maximise their independence, function and quality of life.

• Contributing to discharge planning and ensuring patients have appropriate supports in place before leaving the hospital.

• Assessing the need for equipment, adaptations and other practical supports.

• Carrying out environmental or home assessments where required.

• Providing education, advice and practical guidance to patients, families and carers.

• Working closely with the wider MDT to ensure a coordinated approach to patient care.

• Liaising with community services and other healthcare professionals where appropriate to support continuity of care.

• Maintaining accurate clinical documentation and reports in line with professional and organisational standards.

As a Senior OT, you’ll also have the opportunity to provide clinical support and guidance to junior colleagues and contribute to the ongoing development of the Occupational Therapy service.

About You

We’re looking for an Occupational Therapist who is:

• CORU registered and eligible to practise in Ireland.

• Experienced at Senior Grade level or an experienced Staff Grade OT ready to take the next step.

• Ideally experienced within a hospital, rehabilitation, acute, older persons or community setting.

• Confident carrying out functional assessments and developing evidence-based intervention plans.

• Experienced in discharge planning and working as part of a multidisciplinary team.

• Comfortable managing a varied caseload and working with a good degree of clinical autonomy.

• A strong communicator who can build positive relationships with patients, families and colleagues.

• Passionate about delivering person-centred care and achieving meaningful outcomes for patients.

Why Consider This Role?

You’ll be joining a well-established private hospital with a strong multidisciplinary approach and the opportunity to make a real difference to patients throughout their rehabilitation journey.

The role offers:

• Permanent, full-time employment

• Competitive salary

• Sign-on bonus

• CPD and ongoing training opportunities

• Career development opportunities

• Supportive multidisciplinary environment

STAFF GRADE OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST

Location: Portarlington, Co. Laois
Job Type: Permanent | Full-Time

I’m currently recruiting for a Staff Grade Occupational Therapist to join an established multidisciplinary service in Portarlington.

This is a great opportunity for an OT who wants to work in a role where they can have a genuine impact on the independence, quality of life and day-to-day experiences of the people they support.

The role would suit an Occupational Therapist with an interest in working with individuals with intellectual disabilities and/or autism, and who enjoys a varied caseload rather than a purely clinic-based role.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

You’ll provide a high-quality Occupational Therapy service across assessment, intervention and ongoing support. Your work will include:

• Completing comprehensive OT assessments looking at functional ability, sensory processing, motor skills, cognition and independence in daily activities.

• Developing and implementing individualised OT intervention plans based around the person’s needs and goals.

• Supporting people to develop greater independence in areas such as self-care, daily living, mobility and participation in their home and community.

• Assessing environments and recommending appropriate adaptations, equipment and assistive technology where required.

• Providing advice and practical guidance to families, carers and frontline staff so that OT recommendations can be embedded into everyday support.

• Working closely with a multidisciplinary team and contributing OT expertise to reviews, case conferences and care planning.

• Supporting the development and supervision of Occupational Therapy Assistants.

• Completing clear clinical documentation, professional reports and risk assessments in line with best practice and clinical governance.

• Contributing to Assessment of Need processes and multidisciplinary assessments where appropriate.

• Taking an active role in service development, clinical audits and maintaining high professional standards.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

We’re looking for an Occupational Therapist who is:

• CORU registered and eligible to work as an Occupational Therapist in Ireland.

• Ideally has 1+ years’ post-qualification experience.

Join a fast‑growing SaaS company at a true inflection point. They’re still seed‑stage but have already doubled revenue in six months with only the founder and one AE. With a strong, active pipeline, BDRs in place, and a product that’s clearly resonating in the market, they’re now ready to bring in a Founding AE who can turn this momentum into repeatable, scalable revenue.

This is a founding role: hands‑on, cooperative, and full of ownership. You’ll work directly with the founder, influence the GTM motion, and help build a sales engine that can scale globally. If you thrive in sub‑100‑employee environments where you can move fast, shape the narrative, and genuinely smash it, this is the moment to step in.

🎯 Role Responsibilities

  • Lead the full sales cycle with confidence, clarity, and warmth

  • Shape the pitch and refine the demo, helping define the value story

  • Convert a warm, active pipeline into predictable revenue

  • Build trusted relationships with enterprise and mid‑market stakeholders

  • Partner closely with founders, product, and marketing to influence GTM

  • Bring structure and rhythm to a fast‑moving, high‑growth environment

  • Help set the tone for a supportive, high‑performance sales culture

🧩 What You Bring

  • Experience selling in seed/Series A environments without perfect processes

  • Strong track record selling into sub‑100‑employee companies

  • Confidence navigating complex enterprise and mid‑market deals

  • A cooperative, thoughtful, and curious approach to selling

  • Resilience, adaptability, and a builder’s mindset

  • Comfortable working onsite in Dublin, 5 days/week

  • A desire to grow with the company and shape its future

If you’ve built before, you’ll thrive here.

💰 What’s In It For You

  • Meaningful equity with real upside

  • A chance to join at the perfect inflection point

  • Direct influence on product, GTM, and future hiring

  • A team that values transparency, empathy, and impact

IDFRS1

job.title: Occupational Therapist
job.description:
Discovery & Assessment of Needs Project - Occupational Therapist

Location: North Dublin, with some travel to satellite locations
Duration: Approximately 8 weeks
Contract Type: Project-Based / Temporary
HSE Payscale

We are currently recruiting OTs to join a Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) for an exciting Discovery and Assessment of Needs Project within an adult Disability Team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for professionals who are passionate about person-centred practice, disability rights, social inclusion and supporting people to achieve meaningful life outcomes.

The project will focus on gaining a deeper understanding of the aspirations, goals and support needs of adults who use my client's services. The findings will help inform the future development and redesign of adult services in line with the principles of New Directions, ensuring that supports remain person-centred, evidence-based and focused on individual outcomes.

The Opportunity

Successful candidates will receive structured training and induction from the CRC in the assessment methodology before commencing the project. Ongoing support will also be provided throughout the assignment.

Over approximately 8 weeks, you will undertake scheduled assessments with adults attending services.

Assessments will explore:

  • Individual aspirations, goals and future plans
  • Community participation and social inclusion
  • Supports required to achieve meaningful outcomes
  • Unmet needs and opportunities for further development
  • Individuals' strengths, preferences and personal priorities

Requirements

  • OT Qualification
  • CORU reg
  • Irish working rights
  • Have experience working with adults with disabilities
  • Understand the principles of New Directions and rights-based service delivery
  • Have strong skills in engagement, interviewing, facilitation and information gathering
  • Can effectively engage with adults with diverse communication needs
  • Take a strengths-based and progressive approach to disability support
  • Are passionate about person-centred practice, social inclusion and empowering individuals to achieve their goals
  • Share values centred around respect, collaboration, quality and person-centred support

Interested?

If you are a qualified with relevant disability experience and would like to be considered for this project, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now to find out more about this exciting short-term project opportunity.

Call Isabel 0861449043 for more information.

job.description:
Locum Doctor – Telephone Triage - Emergency Medicine

Dublin or Donegal | Flexible Hours | Excellent Locum Rates

We are currently seeking an experienced Locum Doctor to join a professional clinical team providing telephone triage and clinical assessment.

This is an excellent opportunity for a doctor with an Emergency Medicine background who is looking for flexible locum work in a supportive, professional office environment.

job.title: Senior Process Engineer
job.description:
Our client, a well-established industrial operation based in East Cork, is seeking an experienced Packaging Process Engineer to join their team.

This is a senior engineering role focused on packaging, process optimisation and continuous improvement, with responsibility for providing technical leadership and driving improvements across safety, quality, reliability, efficiency and production performance.

The Role

Reporting to the Engineering & Maintenance Manager, you will take ownership of packaging processes and selected production operations, providing technical expertise and driving continuous improvement.

Key responsibilities include

  • Act as process owner for site packaging operations and selected production processes
  • Provide technical support and troubleshooting for packaging equipment and production processes
  • Analyse OEE, downtime, waste, quality and throughput to identify improvement opportunities
  • Lead root cause investigations and implement effective corrective and preventative solutions
  • Lead continuous improvement and process optimisation initiatives
  • Drive improvements in line performance, changeover efficiency and equipment reliability
  • Establish and maintain effective process control standards
  • Support the introduction, qualification and validation of new packaging formats, materials and equipment
  • Lead and support cost reduction, quality, reliability and debottlenecking projects
  • Work closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Quality and HSE
  • Work with suppliers to resolve packaging material and equipment performance issues
  • Provide technical oversight for selected production processes and support change management activities

What We're Looking For

  • Degree in Chemical, Mechanical, Manufacturing Engineering or a related Engineering discipline
  • Strong experience within a manufacturing, pharmaceutical, food, beverage or packaging environment
  • Proven experience with automated packaging equipment and packaging line operations
  • Strong understanding of process optimisation and continuous improvement
  • Experience analysing OEE, downtime, waste and production performance data
  • Experience leading process improvement and problem-solving initiatives
  • Knowledge of Lean / Six Sigma would be advantageous
  • Knowledge of PLC systems and industrial automation would be beneficial
  • Excellent analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills
  • A proactive, results-driven approach with strong organisational and problem-solving ability

What's On Offer?

  • €80,000 - €91,000 salary
  • Compressive benefits package including Bonus, Healthcare and Pension
  • Permanent position with a well-established industrial operation
  • Senior engineering role with significant ownership and responsibility
  • Opportunity to deliver measurable improvements in efficiency, reliability, quality and cost
  • Excellent long-term career development potential

Apply today for a confidential discussion about this opportunity.

job.title: Senior Sales Executive
job.description:
Senior Sales Executive

Westmeath (Principally based, with territory travel)

Role Overview

This is a pivotal role designed to drive media sales, manage key agency relationships, and help lead the broader sales team. The ideal candidate will be a self-starter who can hit the ground running, secure revenue across our core counties and beyond, and provide strong leadership support within a fast-paced media environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Consistently produce monthly media sales to meet or exceed targets, proactively driving income growth within and outside our traditional franchise area.

  • Maintain, strengthen, and expand productive, high-value relationships with advertising agencies and key direct clients.

  • Assist in expanding the client pool and increasing commercial returns; collaborate on developing innovative marketing products and techniques.

  • Support the Sales Director in coaching, mentoring, and managing field sales personnel, fostering a culture of shared best practices.

  • Act as a dependable senior resource by providing seamless territory cover during staff absences.

  • Manage collections and credit control in accordance with company policy, ensuring all output complies with regulatory codes and best practices.

  • Exceed customer expectations, proactively alerting management to potential standard lapses and recommending remedial actions.

Requirements & Qualifications -Stamp 4 Visa Essential

  • Extensive experience in media sales, advertising, or a fast-paced commercial sales environment (Media/Radio sector experience is a distinct advantage).

  • Demonstrated ability to manage relationship dynamics with advertising agencies and corporate clients.

  • Prior experience or a strong aptitude for coaching, motivating, and supporting sales teams.

  • Strong understanding of sales pipelines, territory management, credit control, and target-driven environments.

  • Must be based within or highly accessible to County Westmeath, with flexibility to travel across territories as required.

job.title: Clinical Sales Executive – Medical Devices & Lab Equipment
job.description:
Clinical Sales Executive – Medical Devices & Lab Equipment

A well-established Irish medical devices company with over 25 years in the market is looking for a Clinical Sales Executive to join their growing commercial team. This is a business with a strong reputation across the Irish healthcare system — the type of place where people stay because the culture backs them up and the results speak for themselves.

The Opportunity

This is a field-based role, covering public hospitals and HSE facilities across your territory, for someone who follows through and delivers, with a strong focus on histology and hospital laboratory departments. You'll be selling instrumentation, consumables, and diagnostics into hospital labs — generating new business, winning tenders, and growing accounts across your patch.

If you already have a network inside Irish hospital labs and experience delivering results in a similar role, this gives you the platform to take on bigger accounts and bigger opportunities.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Owning and growing a territory of public hospital and HSE lab accounts, with a focus on histology departments
  • Leading the tender process end-to-end — pricing, submissions, negotiation, close
  • Selling and demonstrating instrumentation and diagnostics equipment, backed by technical training and support
  • Leveraging existing relationships to generate new business within hospital histology and pathology labs
  • Working with a lean, effective internal team — no corporate red tape
  • Representing the company at conferences and industry events to build pipeline

What You'll Need

  • Experience selling into hospital laboratories, ideally with direct exposure to histology or pathology departments
  • Background in instrumentation and diagnostics sales — you understand the equipment and the buying process
  • An existing network of contacts across Irish hospital labs and HSE procurement
  • Experience managing tender and public procurement processes
  • Full clean driving licence, comfortable covering a national territory

What's In It For You

  • Competitive base + uncapped, achievable commission
  • Company car
  • Laptop & telephone
  • Private healthcare
  • Contributory pension
  • Genuine autonomy and ownership of your territory

Why This One's Worth a Look

This is a stable, family-run business that's been performing well in this space for decades, and they're selective because they want people who deliver.

job.title: Warehouse & Logistics Manager - Agri
job.description:
FRS Recruitment are now inviting applications for the role of Warehouse & Logistics Manager – Agri for our Client who are an Agri Business operating in South Kildare.

About the Role

Our Client is seeking an experienced, highly organised and commercially minded Warehouse Manager to take responsibility for the day-to-day management and development of our new warehouse facility.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who wants to build and shape a warehouse operation from the ground up.

The successful candidate will bring strong experience in warehousing, stock management, order processing and logistics, while also having an interest and ability in using digital systems and technology to improve warehouse efficiency and accuracy.

As Warehouse & Logistics Manager you will also take ownership of the warehouse environment, establish robust processes, introduce appropriate systems and controls, and create a professional, efficient and scalable operation.

This is a hands-on management position for someone who enjoys making things happen and wants to put their own stamp on a warehouse operation.

Key Responsibilities

  • Warehouse Management - Take overall responsibility for the efficient day-to-day running of the warehouse.
  • Digital Systems & Warehouse Technology - Developing the digital capability of the warehouse while assessing and improving the systems currently used to manage warehouse operations.
  • Stock Control & Inventory Management - Maintain accurate records of stock received, transferred, allocated and dispatched.
  • Order Processing & Fulfilment - Manage the end-to-end warehouse order fulfilment process.
  • New Warehouse Set-Up & Development - As we are moving into a new warehouse facility, the successful candidate will have a significant role in designing and establishing the operation.
  • Team Management - Recruit, train and manage warehouse personnel as the operation develops.
  • Health & Safety - Take responsibility for maintaining high health and safety standards within the warehouse while ensuring warehouse procedures comply with relevant legislation and company policies.

Essential Experience

  • Proven experience managing or supervising a warehouse operation.
  • Strong knowledge of stock control and inventory management.
  • Experience with order processing, picking, packing and dispatch.
  • Experience implementing or improving warehouse processes.
  • Strong computer and systems skills.
  • Experience working with ERP, inventory or warehouse management systems.

Desirable Experience

  • Experience setting up or relocating a warehouse.
  • Experience implementing a WMS or ERP system.
  • Experience with barcode scanning or RFID.
  • Experience integrating warehouse systems with sales, purchasing or accounting systems.
  • Experience with agricultural, engineering, machinery, parts or technical products.

Apply:

  • Upload CV using link attached
  • Contact Bonnie on 086 103 8534

All applications treated with strict confidence

job.title: Site Engineer (Water Infrastructure)
job.description:
FRS Recruitment are working with a rapidly growing Civil Engineering Contractor to recruit a Site Engineer for long-term water and civil infrastructure projects across Limerick, North Kerry and West Cork.

This is an excellent opportunity for an Engineer who enjoys the technical and site-based elements of construction, while also looking to broaden their experience across project coordination and management.

The successful candidate will work across a long-term framework contract, delivering essential water infrastructure projects including pumping stations and associated civil works. The position will offer a good combination of site and office-based work, with the majority of time generally spent across live projects.

There is also strong potential for career progression, with the opportunity to develop towards a Junior Project Manager position as experience grows.

Responsibilities

  • Carry out setting out, surveying and engineering checks.
  • Coordinate day-to-day engineering activities across live construction sites.
  • Support delivery of pumping stations and infrastructure projects.
  • Coordinate subcontractors, site teams and construction activities.
  • Assist Project Managers with planning and project coordination.
  • Maintain accurate site records, reports and project documentation.
  • Monitor works against drawings, specifications and quality requirements.
  • Support projects from construction through testing and completion.

Requirements

  • Degree in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Previous civil engineering or construction experience is desirable.
  • Practical setting out experience within a site environment.
  • Total Stations & GPS experience are highly desirable.
  • Strong communication, organisation and problem-solving skills required.
  • Water, utilities or infrastructure experience would be advantageous.
  • Irish or UK construction experience is highly advantageous.
  • Ambition to develop towards project management responsibilities.

Salary & Benefits

  • €50,000 – €65,000+ salary, depending on experience.
  • Company vehicle and fuel card included with package.
  • Pension
  • Phone, Laptop

Futher benefits discussed over a call

job.title: Enterprise Business Development Representive
job.description:
This is not a typical BDR role. You’d be joining a lean, fast‑moving SaaS company that’s scaling, backed by strong funding and a leadership team that wants people who thrive in the chaos of early‑stage growth.

You’ll work directly with the Founding AE, Head of Sales and the Founder helping build the outbound engine that fuels the company’s next funding round.

What You’ll Do

  • Own outbound prospecting into enterprise and mid‑market accounts

  • Build pipeline for AEs working 45‑day sales cycles with in average 80K deal sizes

  • Research, identify, and engage multiple stakeholders across complex organisations

  • Partner closely with AEs to shape messaging, demos, and outbound strategy

  • Work with leadership who value hunger, solutions, and zero‑ego collaboration

  • Bring ideas, challenge processes, and help build the sales playbook from scratch

  • Thrive in a busy, hands‑on, 5‑days‑onsite environment where everyone pulls in the same direction

Why This Role Matters

The company is aggressively hiring BDRs because outbound is the engine of their growth. You’re not just booking meetings — you’re shaping the future of the sales organisation.

You’ll be joining at a moment where:

  • The team is small, so your impact is huge

  • Leadership is accessible and wants people who speak up

  • There’s real opportunity to move into AE as the team scales

  • Equity grows with each funding round

  • You’ll learn full‑cycle sales from people who’ve built engines before

What They’re Looking For

  • An ambitious sales person who wants to grow fast

  • Someone who loves outbound and isn’t afraid of volume

  • A problem‑solver who brings solutions, not complaints

  • Someone who enjoys the chaos of a startup and wants to help build

  • A communicator who can handle multiple stakeholders

  • Someone competitive, driven, and hungry to progress

What You Get

  • Competitive base salary + strong commission

  • Meaningful equity that grows with each round

  • Direct mentorship from AEs and leadership

  • A chance to move into AE as the team scales

  • A culture that rewards effort, honesty, and ambition

  • Being part of a company protecting global brands

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Senior or Lead HSEQ professional looking to move beyond a predominantly site-based position, with greater involvement across pre-construction, PQQs, tender submissions and wider HSEQ strategy.

The successful candidate will work across a diverse portfolio of infrastructure projects incorporating Civil, Structural and M&E works, supporting both pre-construction and operational teams from tender stage through to project delivery.

Salary & Benefits

job.title: People Change Advisor
job.description:
People Change Advisor - Swords, Dublin

Hybrid Flexibility: 1 - 2 days per week office based.

Permanent Full Time

Salary: €45,000 - €50,000 plus pension, bonus and 25 days AL

Overview:

The People Change Advisor will support the delivery of TUPE transfers, acquisitions, restructures, redundancies, and other organisational change activities across the Ireland and UK business. As the TUPE and Change subject matter expert, you will provide practical advice and guidance to managers, ensuring change programmes are delivered effectively, compliantly, and with a positive employee experience at their core.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage a high-volume caseload of TUPE and organisational change projects.
  • Lead end-to-end TUPE transfers, ensuring legal compliance and adherence to deadlines.
  • Coordinate Employee Liability Information (ELI) and mobilisation activities.
  • Support and attend consultation and welcome meetings across Ireland as required.
  • Advise managers on TUPE, redundancy, restructuring, and organisational change processes.
  • Produce redundancy calculations and change-related documentation.
  • Review business cases and identify potential commercial and employee relations risks.
  • Coach and train managers on people change matters.
  • Support employee engagement throughout change programmes.

Skills / Qualifications:

  • Proven HR experience in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong TUPE experience and knowledge of employment legislation.
  • Experience managing redundancy, restructuring, and organisational change processes.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills.

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Senior Respiratory Physiologist to join a progressive and expanding Respiratory Physiology Department within a leading private healthcare provider in Galway.

We are seeking a highly motivated and patient-focused professional with significant experience in sleep diagnostics and respiratory physiology laboratory services. The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering high-quality diagnostic investigations while supporting the continued development of an advanced respiratory and sleep service.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform and interpret a comprehensive range of respiratory physiology investigations, including spirometry, lung volumes, gas transfer (DLCO), bronchial challenge testing and overnight oximetry.
  • Lead and deliver high-quality sleep diagnostic services, including the setup, scoring and interpretation of ambulatory and laboratory-based sleep studies.
  • Demonstrate expertise in the investigation and management pathway for sleep-disordered breathing, including CPAP initiation, troubleshooting and patient education.
  • Ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the respiratory physiology and sleep laboratory, maintaining the highest standards of quality assurance and equipment calibration.
  • Work collaboratively with Respiratory Consultants, Sleep Physicians and the multidisciplinary team to provide an efficient, patient-centred diagnostic service.
  • Maintain accurate clinical records and prepare detailed technical reports.
  • Participate in service development, clinical audit and implementation of best practice.
  • Support, mentor and supervise junior physiologists and contribute to ongoing staff education and training.

Essential Requirements

  • Degree in Clinical Measurement Science, Clinical Physiology or an equivalent recognised qualification.
  • Eligibility for professional registration/accreditation relevant to respiratory physiology.
  • A minimum of five years' post-qualification experience in respiratory physiology.
  • Extensive experience in performing and analysing respiratory function tests.
  • Significant experience in sleep diagnostics, including polysomnography and cardiorespiratory sleep studies.
  • Experience working within a dedicated respiratory physiology and sleep laboratory.
  • Excellent knowledge of quality assurance, laboratory standards and equipment maintenance.
  • Strong organisational, communication and leadership skills.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Candidates must have current permission to work in Ireland or be eligible to obtain the appropriate employment permit and registration required to work in Ireland.

Desirable

  • Experience with CPAP therapy initiation and follow-up clinics.
  • Previous experience supervising or mentoring staff.
  • Participation in clinical audit, research or service improvement initiatives.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • A modern, well-equipped respiratory physiology and sleep laboratory.
  • Opportunities for continuing professional development and further specialist training.
  • A supportive multidisciplinary team committed to delivering excellence in patient care.
  • Career progression within a dynamic and expanding healthcare environment.

If you are an experienced Respiratory Physiologist with a passion for sleep medicine and advanced respiratory diagnostics, apply online for an immediate interview.

Accounts Payable & Invoice Processing

Reconciliations & Month-End Support

General Administration

job.title: Senior Radiation Therapist
job.description:
Senior Radiation Therapist

Shape the Future of Cancer Care

An exceptional opportunity has arisen for experienced Senior Radiation Therapists to join a brand-new, purpose-built cancer centre in the Midwest of Ireland.

This is more than a new role—it's a chance to be part of a pioneering team from the beginning, helping to establish one of Ireland's most modern radiotherapy services and delivering world-class care to patients.

Why Join?

As a Senior Radiation Therapist, you will play a key role in developing and delivering advanced radiotherapy services within a collaborative, patient-centred environment.

Advanced Clinical Practice

Work at the forefront of radiotherapy, with opportunities to develop expertise in:

  • Stereotactic Radiotherapy (SRT/SABR)
  • Advanced treatment planning
  • Image-guided radiotherapy (IGRT)
  • Modern radiotherapy technologies and techniques
  • Varian radiotherapy system

Career Development

Commitment to investing in people and supporting long-term career growth through:

  • Clear career progression pathways
  • Leadership and management development opportunities
  • Specialist clinical roles
  • Ongoing professional education and funded training

Research & Innovation

Become part of a service committed to advancing cancer care through:

  • Participation in national and international clinical trials
  • Research collaboration and service development
  • Opportunities to contribute to innovation and evidence-based practice
  • Support for academic development and conference participation

What's On Offer

Exceptional people deserve exceptional support.

A comprehensive package will attract the best Radiation Therapists and includes:

  • Competitive salary plus premium payments and performance pay
  • Attractive benefits package
  • Generous relocation support for successful candidates moving to the region
  • Excellent annual leave entitlement
  • Pension scheme
  • Continuous professional development funding
  • Supportive multidisciplinary working environment
  • Access to the latest radiotherapy technologies within a newly developed facility

About You

You are an experienced Radiation Therapist who is passionate about delivering outstanding patient care and eager to contribute to the development of an innovative cancer service.

You will bring:

  • Significant post-registration experience in radiation therapy
  • Strong clinical knowledge and leadership capability
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills
  • A commitment to quality, patient safety and continuous improvement
  • Enthusiasm for innovation, education and professional development

Be Part of Something New

This is a unique opportunity to help build a new service, influence future practice and make a lasting impact on cancer care in Ireland.

If you are looking for the next step in your career—where advanced practice, research, leadership and innovation come together - we would love to hear from you.

Emma Fenton is a specialist healthcare recruiter with 20 years experience. Applications and informal contact will be treated in strictest confidence.

job.title: Finance Administrator
job.description:
Finance Administrator

Role Purpose

Reporting to the Financial Controller, the Finance Administrator will provide essential support across the day-to-day financial operations of Aoibhneas. The successful candidate will be responsible for a range of financial administration activities, including transaction processing, reconciliations, record maintenance and general finance support.

This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional with strong attention to detail and a proactive approach to contribute to the effective running of the organisation’s finance function.

Flexibility in working hours may be required to meet the needs of the organisation and support the efficient operation of the finance function.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain and update accurate financial records using Sage accounting software.
  • Process accounts payable transactions and complete supplier reconciliations.
  • Prepare and monitor payment schedules, ensuring suppliers are paid accurately and on time.
  • Record receipts and banking transactions and reconcile these against bank statements.
  • Process receipts across various income channels, complete reconciliations and prepare relevant control accounts.
  • Reconcile and post petty cash transactions.
  • Assist with employee expense tracking, verification and processing.
  • Support month-end financial procedures, including reconciliations and journal postings.
  • Assist with the preparation of monthly management accounts and ad hoc financial reports as required.
  • Provide general administrative support to the finance function.
  • Carry out any other duties as assigned by the Financial Controller.

Candidate Requirements

Essential Criteria

  • Third-level qualification in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or a related discipline.
  • Minimum of one year’s relevant experience in a finance, accounts, bookkeeping or administrative role.
  • Proficiency in accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
  • Strong understanding of bookkeeping principles, financial processes and accurate financial record-keeping.
  • Previous experience in accounts payable, supplier reconciliations and processing financial transactions.
  • Experience handling confidential information and maintaining accurate financial records.
  • Excellent organisational skills with a strong focus on accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritise effectively and manage competing workloads to meet deadlines.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to liaise professionally with suppliers, colleagues and external stakeholders.
  • Strong administration and time-management skills.
  • A proactive and flexible approach, with the ability to adapt to changing priorities.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience working with financial systems and databases.
  • Experience preparing financial reports and reconciliations.
  • Previous experience within the not-for-profit or charity sector.
  • Full driving licence.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and adaptability.
  • High levels of integrity and professionalism.
  • Strong sense of dependability and accountability.
  • Strong customer service orientation.
  • Ability to work independently and demonstrate initiative.
  • Ability to work effectively under pressure and consistently meet deadlines.

Personal Attributes

The successful candidate will be:

  • Professional, trustworthy and committed to maintaining confidentiality and financial integrity.
  • A strong communicator who can build positive working relationships with colleagues, suppliers and external stakeholders.
  • Highly organised, accurate and detail oriented.
  • Reliable, proactive and solution-focused, with a positive approach to their work.
  • Comfortable working independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team environment.
  • An effective time manager who can balance competing priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Someone who demonstrates initiative, sound judgement and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Employee Benefits

Aoibhneas offers a supportive working environment with a range of benefits, including:

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two well-being days, with additional incremental days in line with length of service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme (EAP).

job.title: Education & Training Officer
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Education & Training Officer to lead the development and delivery of education, training and awareness initiatives across the organisation and wider community.

Role Purpose

The Education & Training Officer will develop and deliver high-quality training and awareness programmes that promote understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women, children and young people.

The role will build knowledge and skills across Aoibhneas, partner organisations and the wider community through training, education, awareness initiatives and professional engagement. The postholder will also represent the organisation and contribute to service development and best practice.

Key Responsibilities

Education & Training

  • Develop, coordinate and deliver training for staff, volunteers, students and external stakeholders.
  • Design and maintain training materials, presentations, guidance and learning resources.
  • Deliver training on domestic abuse, safeguarding, trauma-informed practice, coercive control, risk assessment, child protection and related areas.
  • Develop annual training plans aligned with organisational priorities and legislative requirements.
  • Evaluate training effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Maintain accurate training records and support compliance with mandatory learning requirements.
  • Work with managers to identify learning and development needs.

Community Awareness & Engagement

  • Deliver workshops, presentations, information sessions and awareness initiatives to schools, community groups, statutory agencies and voluntary organisations.
  • Promote understanding of domestic abuse and best practice responses within communities and professional networks.
  • Represent Aoibhneas at conferences, forums, community events and professional networks.
  • Develop accessible educational and information resources.
  • Support local and national awareness initiatives relating to domestic abuse and violence against women.

Service Development

  • Research emerging trends, evidence and best practice to inform training and programme development.
  • Identify training and knowledge gaps across services and partner organisations.
  • Contribute to the development of policies, procedures and practice guidance.
  • Support specialist programmes for women, children and young people affected by domestic abuse.
  • Contribute to quality improvement and organisational learning.

Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop and maintain positive relationships with statutory agencies, schools, colleges, community organisations and professional networks.
  • Support collaborative initiatives and referral pathways.
  • Participate in relevant interagency groups, committees and professional networks.
  • Strengthen partnership approaches to domestic abuse prevention and response.

Administration & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of training delivery, attendance and outcomes.
  • Prepare reports, statistics and evaluation data.
  • Assist with funding reports, monitoring requirements and service evaluations.
  • Maintain training databases and learning management systems where applicable.
  • Liaise with the Head of Services regarding priorities and programme development.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Degree-level qualification in Education, Training, Social Care, Community Development, Social Science, Adult Education or a related discipline.
  • Minimum three years' relevant experience in training, education, social care, community development or a related setting.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women and children.
  • Proven experience designing, delivering and evaluating training programmes.
  • Excellent facilitation, presentation and communication skills.
  • Experience developing training materials and learning resources.
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills.
  • Excellent report-writing and data management abilities.
  • Experience working with partners and external stakeholders.
  • Full driving licence.

Desirable

  • Qualification or accreditation in training/adult education.
  • Knowledge of Children First and safeguarding requirements.
  • Experience delivering training within the domestic abuse, social care or community sector.

job.title: Education & Training Officer
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Education & Training Officer to lead the development and delivery of education, training and awareness initiatives across the organisation and wider community.

Role Purpose

The Education & Training Officer will develop and deliver high-quality training and awareness programmes that promote understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women, children and young people.

The role will build knowledge and skills across Aoibhneas, partner organisations and the wider community through training, education, awareness initiatives and professional engagement. The postholder will also represent the organisation and contribute to service development and best practice.

Key Responsibilities

Education & Training

  • Develop, coordinate and deliver training for staff, volunteers, students and external stakeholders.
  • Design and maintain training materials, presentations, guidance and learning resources.
  • Deliver training on domestic abuse, safeguarding, trauma-informed practice, coercive control, risk assessment, child protection and related areas.
  • Develop annual training plans aligned with organisational priorities and legislative requirements.
  • Evaluate training effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Maintain accurate training records and support compliance with mandatory learning requirements.
  • Work with managers to identify learning and development needs.

Community Awareness & Engagement

  • Deliver workshops, presentations, information sessions and awareness initiatives to schools, community groups, statutory agencies and voluntary organisations.
  • Promote understanding of domestic abuse and best practice responses within communities and professional networks.
  • Represent Aoibhneas at conferences, forums, community events and professional networks.
  • Develop accessible educational and information resources.
  • Support local and national awareness initiatives relating to domestic abuse and violence against women.

Service Development

  • Research emerging trends, evidence and best practice to inform training and programme development.
  • Identify training and knowledge gaps across services and partner organisations.
  • Contribute to the development of policies, procedures and practice guidance.
  • Support specialist programmes for women, children and young people affected by domestic abuse.
  • Contribute to quality improvement and organisational learning.

Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop and maintain positive relationships with statutory agencies, schools, colleges, community organisations and professional networks.
  • Support collaborative initiatives and referral pathways.
  • Participate in relevant interagency groups, committees and professional networks.
  • Strengthen partnership approaches to domestic abuse prevention and response.

Administration & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of training delivery, attendance and outcomes.
  • Prepare reports, statistics and evaluation data.
  • Assist with funding reports, monitoring requirements and service evaluations.
  • Maintain training databases and learning management systems where applicable.
  • Liaise with the Head of Services regarding priorities and programme development.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Degree-level qualification in Education, Training, Social Care, Community Development, Social Science, Adult Education or a related discipline.
  • Minimum three years' relevant experience in training, education, social care, community development or a related setting.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women and children.
  • Proven experience designing, delivering and evaluating training programmes.
  • Excellent facilitation, presentation and communication skills.
  • Experience developing training materials and learning resources.
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills.
  • Excellent report-writing and data management abilities.
  • Experience working with partners and external stakeholders.
  • Full driving licence.

Desirable

  • Qualification or accreditation in training/adult education.
  • Knowledge of Children First and safeguarding requirements.
  • Experience delivering training within the domestic abuse, social care or community sector.
  • Experience of interagency working.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Integrity and dependability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.
  • Strong self-management and emotional resilience.

Role Requirements

The role will require flexibility to work across Aoibhneas and community locations, with regular travel to educational, community and organisational settings.

Working hours will generally be five days per week between 9.00am and 6.00pm, with occasional evening or weekend work required to facilitate training, awareness events and community engagement activities.

A full driving licence is essential.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.
