job.title: Facilities Supervisor
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Facilities Supervisor to oversee the maintenance, safety, security and operational management of Aoibhneas properties, facilities and accommodation sites.

Facilities Management

  • Oversee the day-to-day management and maintenance of Aoibhneas properties, accommodation units, offices and service locations.
  • Ensure premises are safe, secure, well maintained and fit for purpose.
  • Develop and manage preventative maintenance schedules and conduct regular site inspections.
  • Coordinate repairs, maintenance and refurbishment works.
  • Manage access control, keyholding and building security arrangements.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance, inspection, servicing and compliance records.

Health, Safety & Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with relevant Health & Safety legislation and organisational policies.
  • Conduct and review risk assessments relating to buildings, equipment and workplace activities.
  • Monitor fire safety systems, emergency lighting, alarms, extinguishers and evacuation procedures.
  • Ensure statutory inspections, certifications and servicing are completed and recorded.
  • Support emergency planning and business continuity arrangements.
  • Investigate and report facilities-related incidents, hazards, accidents and near misses.
  • Promote a strong culture of safety and continuous improvement.

Contractor & Supplier Management

  • Source, appoint and manage contractors and service providers in line with procurement requirements.
  • Monitor contractor performance, service agreements, costs and value for money.
  • Ensure contractors comply with Health & Safety, safeguarding and organisational requirements.
  • Obtain quotations and support facilities-related procurement.
  • Maintain effective relationships with suppliers, landlords, maintenance providers and utility companies.

Asset & Resource Management

  • Maintain an accurate asset register across all sites.
  • Oversee furniture, equipment, fixtures and operational supplies.
  • Plan asset and equipment replacement programmes.
  • Support budgeting, forecasting and monitoring of facilities expenditure.
  • Ensure effective use of facilities resources and budgets.

Projects & Administration

  • Support refurbishment, relocation, property acquisition and capital improvement projects.
  • Liaise with internal teams, contractors, consultants and regulatory bodies.
  • Monitor project timelines, budgets and deliverables.
  • Maintain accurate facilities records, policies, procedures and compliance documentation.
  • Prepare reports for management on facilities performance, compliance and risks.
  • Support inspections, audits and information requests.
  • Maintain effective systems for logging and monitoring maintenance requests.

Leadership & Support

  • Provide guidance and supervision to facilities, maintenance and contracted personnel as required.
  • Support managers in resolving facilities-related issues.
  • Promote effective communication and collaboration across teams and locations.
  • Contribute to organisational planning and service development.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Relevant third-level qualification in Facilities Management, Property Management, Building Services, Health & Safety, Construction Management or a related discipline, or significant equivalent experience.
  • Minimum three years’ experience in facilities, property or operational management.
  • Experience managing multiple sites and competing priorities.
  • Strong knowledge of Health & Safety legislation and compliance requirements.
  • Experience managing contractors, service providers and maintenance programmes.
  • Strong organisational, planning and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience monitoring budgets and managing resources.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and electronic record management systems.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound operational decisions.

Desirable

  • Health & Safety qualification.
  • Facilities Management qualification.
  • Experience in the community, social care, housing or not-for-profit sector.
  • Project management experience.
  • Experience overseeing refurbishment or capital projects.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Integrity and dependability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.

Role Requirements

The role requires regular travel between Aoibhneas properties and service locations, with the ability to manage competing operational priorities across multiple sites.

Working hours will generally be Monday to Friday; however, flexibility is required to respond to urgent maintenance, compliance or operational matters when necessary.

A full clean driving licence and access to transport are essential.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: Receptionist
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Receptionist to provide high-quality reception, administrative and operational support across the organisation.

Role Purpose

The Administrator / Receptionist will be the first point of contact for visitors, service users, stakeholders and partner agencies, providing a professional, welcoming and efficient service.

The role will support the smooth day-to-day operation of Aoibhneas through reception and office administration, record management, data entry, facilities coordination and stakeholder communication, while maintaining high standards of confidentiality, professionalism and safeguarding.

Key Responsibilities

Reception & Front of House

  • Act as the first point of contact for visitors, clients, stakeholders and external agencies.
  • Manage incoming calls, emails and correspondence, directing enquiries appropriately.
  • Welcome visitors and ensure safeguarding, security and visitor procedures are followed.
  • Maintain reception, meeting rooms and public areas to a professional standard.
  • Manage incoming and outgoing post, deliveries and courier services.
  • Provide information and assistance in a professional, respectful and sensitive manner.

Administration

  • Provide administrative support to the CEO, Head of Services and managers as required.
  • Prepare correspondence, reports, presentations, agendas and other documentation.
  • Maintain accurate electronic and paper filing systems.
  • Manage data entry, document control and record-keeping.
  • Maintain databases and support reporting requirements.
  • Coordinate meetings, room bookings and diaries.
  • Record meeting notes and assist with minutes where required.
  • Support managers with reports, audits and monitoring returns.

Office & Operational Support

  • Order office supplies and monitor stock levels across organisational locations.
  • Liaise with suppliers, contractors and service providers.
  • Support facilities-related requests, including maintenance, repairs and equipment servicing.
  • Assist with Health & Safety administration and compliance documentation.
  • Support procurement activities and value-for-money purchasing.

Information Management & GDPR

  • Maintain accurate, secure and up-to-date records.
  • Support compliance with GDPR, confidentiality requirements and organisational policies.
  • Handle sensitive information appropriately and maintain the confidentiality of service users and stakeholders.
  • Support the management of organisational databases and reporting systems.

Stakeholder & Service Support

  • Build positive working relationships with service users, staff, service providers, funders, contractors and community partners.
  • Assist with the coordination of meetings, events, training and organisational activities.
  • Support effective communication and information sharing across the organisation.
  • Assist service teams with data collection, monitoring and reporting.
  • Support staff with administrative requirements relating to service delivery.
  • Assist with onboarding, document management and organisational projects.

Other Duties

  • Participate in relevant training and professional development.
  • Work collaboratively across all departments and service teams.
  • Ensure organisational policies, procedures and legislative requirements are followed.
  • Work under the direction of the CEO, Head of Services or designated officer.
  • Undertake other duties appropriate to the role as required.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Qualification in Administration, Office Administration, Reception, Public Administration or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Minimum two years' experience in an administrative, reception or customer-facing role.
  • Excellent organisational and administrative skills.
  • Strong planning, time-management and multitasking abilities.
  • Excellent IT skills, including Microsoft Office and database systems.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills.
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Ability to prioritise workload and meet deadlines.

Desirable

  • Experience within a social care, community, charity or not-for-profit environment.
  • Experience using CRM or case management systems.
  • Experience supporting governance, compliance or reporting processes.
  • Experience coordinating suppliers and contractors.
  • Experience supporting office or facilities management.
  • Experience in report writing and data management.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.
  • Strong problem-solving skills.

Role Requirements

Working hours will generally be Monday to Friday, five days per week. Flexibility may be required to support organisational events, meetings and service requirements.

The postholder may also be required to work across different Aoibhneas locations from time to time.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: Key Workers
job.description:
FRS Recruitment in Partnership with Aoibhneas

Role: Key Workers

Contract: Full-Time - Permanent - 39 Hours

Salary: €40,851 per annum

Location: North Dublin/ Finglas Based

The Key Worker role involves welcoming new families into the service and ensure the provision of practical and emotional supports. Key workers will provide emergency accommodation to Women and Children fleeing Domestic Abuse and provide support and structured services to residents in Refuge and Community settings, operating the 24-hour free Helpline, carrying out assessments of support needs; providing information, advocacy and referral services.

Key Responsibilities including, but not limited to:

Client Services

  • Make an initial assessment of a client’s support needs via the refuge/ drop-in/helpline service.
  • Provide information, advocacy and referrals to appropriate services.
  • Work collaboratively with statutory and voluntary agencies.

Linkages

  • Develop referral links for clients with local support services and networks.
  • Develop links with local service providers.

Administration

  • Maintain and manage all client case records to a high professional standard, ensuring all information is accurately documented and updated.
  • Ensure standards are maintained and adhered to in line with policy, procedure and legislation.

Essential Requirements:

  • Third Level Qualification at degree level in social science, social care or related field.
  • A minimum of 1 year relevant work experience working in a social care setting with women/ families.
  • Experience of key-working clients or individual case-work.
  • Excellent knowledge and understanding of domestic violence and issues affecting women and children experiencing domestic violence.
  • Excellent knowledge and practical understanding of child protection, child welfare and safeguarding principles, including the ability to recognise, respond to, record and report child protection and welfare concerns in line with Children First legislation, organisational policy and best practice.
  • Understanding and working knowledge of Domestic Violence Act/ Children’s First Legislation/ Child Care Act.
  • Excellent facilitation, training and communication skills.

Desirable Criteria:

  • Experience of inter-agency working
  • Full driving License

job.title: Finance Administrator
job.description:
FRS is proud to partner with Aoibhneas on this recruitment campaign and welcomes applications from candidates who are passionate about delivering high-quality financial administration within a values-led organisation

Role Purpose

Reporting to the Financial Controller, the Finance Administrator will provide essential support across the day-to-day financial operations of Aoibhneas. The successful candidate will be responsible for a range of financial administration activities, including transaction processing, reconciliations, record maintenance and general finance support.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain accurate financial records using Sage.
  • Process accounts payable, supplier reconciliations and payment schedules.
  • Record and reconcile receipts, banking and petty cash transactions.
  • Process income receipts and maintain relevant control accounts.
  • Assist with employee expenses, month-end reconciliations and journal postings.
  • Support the preparation of monthly management accounts and financial reports.
  • Provide general administrative support to the finance team.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Financial Controller.

Candidate Requirements

Essential Criteria

  • Third-level qualification in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration or a related discipline.
  • Minimum of one year’s relevant experience in a finance, accounts, bookkeeping or administrative role.
  • Proficiency in accounting software and Microsoft Excel.
  • Strong understanding of bookkeeping principles, financial processes and accurate financial record-keeping.
  • Previous experience in accounts payable, supplier reconciliations and processing financial transactions.
  • Experience handling confidential information and maintaining accurate financial records.
  • Ability to work independently, prioritise effectively and manage competing workloads to meet deadlines.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to liaise professionally with suppliers, colleagues and external stakeholders.
  • Strong administration and time-management skills.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience working with financial systems and databases.
  • Experience preparing financial reports and reconciliations.
  • Previous experience within the not-for-profit or charity sector.
  • Full driving licence.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and adaptability.
  • High levels of integrity and professionalism.

Employee Benefits

Aoibhneas offers a supportive working environment with a range of benefits, including:

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two well-being days, with additional incremental days in line with length of service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme (EAP).

job.title: Housekeeping Staff - Part time
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a reliable and hardworking Housekeeper to support the cleanliness, hygiene, safety and overall presentation of Aoibhneas premises. This role is a part time role for 20 hours.

Role Purpose

The Housekeeper will be responsible for maintaining a high standard of cleanliness across Aoibhneas accommodation and facilities, ensuring a safe, comfortable and welcoming environment for residents, staff and visitors.

The role will involve general cleaning, maintaining cleaning supplies, supporting room turnarounds and ensuring all assigned areas are kept clean, organised and hygienic. The successful candidate will also have a basic understanding of Health & Safety procedures.

Key Responsibilities

  • Carry out general cleaning duties across Aoibhneas premises and locations.
  • Clean floors, rooms, windows, surfaces and other areas to a high standard.
  • Clean and sanitise bathrooms and restrooms, including replenishing supplies and emptying waste.
  • Vacuum, sweep, mop, dust and maintain assigned areas.
  • Maintain adequate stocks of cleaning products, linen and other housekeeping supplies.
  • Ensure cleaning equipment and supplies are stored safely and maintained appropriately.
  • Transport, replace and manage linen as required.
  • Assist with the cleaning and preparation of residential rooms, including changing beds and preparing accommodation for new residents.
  • Maintain high standards of hygiene, cleanliness and organisation throughout all assigned areas.
  • Follow relevant Health & Safety procedures and report any hazards or maintenance issues.
  • Carry out other housekeeping duties as required.

Person Requirements

  • Previous cleaning or housekeeping experience is desirable.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining high standards.
  • Good organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks effectively.
  • Ability to work within set timeframes and remain calm under pressure.
  • Proactive, reliable and positive approach to work.
  • Good communication skills and the ability to interact respectfully with residents, colleagues and visitors.
  • Basic understanding of Health & Safety requirements.
  • Ability to use initiative and work with minimal supervision.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: HR Administrator
job.description:
FRS Recruitment in Partnership with Aoibhneas

The HR Administrator will play an important role in supporting the HR Coordinator in the effective delivery of HR services across Aoibhneas locations. This is a varied role, providing administrative support across the full employee life cycle and helping to ensure that HR processes are delivered efficiently, accurately, and in line with organisational policies, employment legislation, GDPR requirements, and best practice.

The successful candidate will have excellent organisational and administrative skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage confidential information with discretion and professionalism.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide day-to-day HR administrative support across the full employee life cycle.
  • Support the implementation, maintenance, and ongoing development of the organisation's HR Information System (HRIS), ensuring employee records are accurate and up to date.
  • Maintain employee information, contracts, personnel files, and HR databases in accordance with GDPR requirements and organisational policies.
  • Assist with the review and development of HR systems, processes, policies, and procedures, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and the employee experience.
  • Act as a point of contact for HR-related queries, providing appropriate guidance and support to employees and managers.
  • Coordinate recruitment administration, including vacancy advertising, interview scheduling, candidate correspondence, reference checks, and on boarding documentation.
  • Support on boarding, induction, probation review processes, and employee off boarding, including the coordination of exit interviews.
  • Assist with the administration and coordination of employee benefits, the Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), and employee well-being initiatives.
  • Support employee engagement initiatives, including employee surveys, staff events, and internal communications, in collaboration with the Communications Officer.
  • Maintain HR compliance records and support adherence to employment legislation, organisational policies, and best practice.
  • Assist the HR Coordinator with the preparation of HR reports, metrics, and management information.
  • Coordinate mandatory training, maintain accurate training records, and assist with the development and distribution of training materials.
  • Support performance management processes, including probation reviews, performance appraisals, and learning and development initiatives.
  • Provide administrative support in relation to employee relations matters, ensuring accurate documentation and strict confidentiality at all times.
  • Update the staff intranet as required.
  • Ensure all HR administration is completed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with GDPR and confidentiality requirements.
  • Undertake any other duties appropriate to the role as reasonably requested by the HR Coordinator, Head of Services, or CEO.

Candidate Requirements

Essential Criteria

  • A relevant third-level qualification in Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Administration, Employment Studies, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • A minimum of one year's experience in an HR administration or HR support role.
  • Demonstrable experience supporting key HR functions.
  • Working knowledge of Irish employment legislation and HR best practice.
  • Excellent administrative, organisational, and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage professionally and confidently with employees, managers, and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
  • Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy when maintaining records and preparing HR documentation.
  • A strong understanding of confidentiality, GDPR, and the importance of handling sensitive employee information.

Desirable Criteria

  • Previous experience working within the not-for-profit, charity, social care, or community sector.
  • Experience using HR Information Systems, particularly Sage HR and/or BrightHR.
  • Experience supporting recruitment campaigns, interviews, and candidate on boarding.
  • Knowledge of Garda Vetting, compliance monitoring, and employee file audits.
  • Experience assisting with payroll preparation and benefits administration.
  • Experience supporting HR projects and employee engagement initiatives.
  • A full, clean driving licence and access to transport to facilitate occasional travel between locations.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently, while also contributing effectively as part of a wider team.

Employee Benefits

  • Employer pension contribution of 5%.
  • 22 days' annual leave, including two well-being days, with incremental additional days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to external supervision and an Employee Assistance Programme.

All offers of employment with Aoibhneas are subject to Garda Vetting, satisfactory reference checks, and verification of legal eligibility to work in Ireland. Aoibhneas is an equal opportunities employer. A panel may be formed from this recruitment process.

job.title: EHS Coordinator
job.description:
Are you an experienced EHS Coordinator with strong Permit to Work and contractor management experience looking for your next opportunity in Cork?

Our client, a well-established manufacturing company based in Little Island, Cork, is seeking an EHS Coordinator to join their EHS team. Reporting to the EHS Manager, this is a key site-based role with a particular focus on managing third-party contractors and ensuring safe, compliant execution of works on site.

What you will be doing:

  • Managing and issuing Safe Work Permits / Permit to Work for maintenance, contractor and project activities.
  • Coordinating and monitoring third-party contractors to ensure full compliance with site EHS requirements.
  • Reviewing method statements, risk assessments and safe systems of work before work commences.
  • Ensuring contractors adhere to PPE requirements, site procedures and controls for life-critical activities.
  • Supporting safety investigations, incident reporting and the implementation of corrective actions.
  • Monitoring EHS performance and driving improvements through site KPIs and action plans.
  • Supporting Management of Change (MOC), safety reviews and the development of safe working procedures.
  • Supporting environmental compliance, including waste and wastewater activities.

What we are looking for:

  • Higher Diploma in Safety, Health and Welfare at Work or equivalent.
  • Previous experience in an EHS / Health & Safety role within a manufacturing or regulated environment.
  • Proven experience with Permit to Work / Safe Work Permit systems is essential.
  • Experience managing and coordinating third-party contractors on a manufacturing site.
  • Strong knowledge of risk assessments, method statements and safe systems of work.
  • Experience within a GMP or similarly regulated environment would be advantageous.
  • Strong communication, organisational and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to challenge unsafe practices and hold others accountable.

What is on offer:

  • Competitive salary based on experience.
  • Comprehensive benefits package.
  • Monday to Friday, days-only role.
  • Excellent career development opportunities.
  • Long-term opportunity with a well-established manufacturing organisation.
  • A key role working closely with the EHS Manager and wider site teams.

If you are an experienced EHS Coordinator / Health & Safety professional with strong Permit to Work and contractor management experience, and are looking for a Monday to Friday, days-only opportunity in Little Island, Cork, apply today with your CV.

job.title: Occupational Therapist
job.description:
Discovery & Assessment of Needs Project - Occupational Therapist

Location: North Dublin, with some travel to satellite locations
Duration: Approximately 8 weeks
Contract Type: Project-Based / Temporary
HSE Payscale

We are currently recruiting OTs to join a Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) for an exciting Discovery and Assessment of Needs Project within an adult Disability Team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for professionals who are passionate about person-centred practice, disability rights, social inclusion and supporting people to achieve meaningful life outcomes.

The project will focus on gaining a deeper understanding of the aspirations, goals and support needs of adults who use my client's services. The findings will help inform the future development and redesign of adult services in line with the principles of New Directions, ensuring that supports remain person-centred, evidence-based and focused on individual outcomes.

The Opportunity

Successful candidates will receive structured training and induction from the CRC in the assessment methodology before commencing the project. Ongoing support will also be provided throughout the assignment.

Over approximately 8 weeks, you will undertake scheduled assessments with adults attending services.

Assessments will explore:

  • Individual aspirations, goals and future plans
  • Community participation and social inclusion
  • Supports required to achieve meaningful outcomes
  • Unmet needs and opportunities for further development
  • Individuals' strengths, preferences and personal priorities

Requirements

  • OT Qualification
  • CORU reg
  • Irish working rights
  • Have experience working with adults with disabilities
  • Understand the principles of New Directions and rights-based service delivery
  • Have strong skills in engagement, interviewing, facilitation and information gathering
  • Can effectively engage with adults with diverse communication needs
  • Take a strengths-based and progressive approach to disability support
  • Are passionate about person-centred practice, social inclusion and empowering individuals to achieve their goals
  • Share values centred around respect, collaboration, quality and person-centred support

Interested?

If you are a qualified with relevant disability experience and would like to be considered for this project, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now to find out more about this exciting short-term project opportunity.

Call Isabel 0861449043 for more information.

job.title: Store Manager
job.description:
Store Manager (Supermarket) - North Co. Galway

You will positively contribute to all aspects of managing the store, including the delivery of budgeted sales and profit targets, shrinkage/waste control, personnel costs, overall standards, procedures and disciplines across all departments.

Key Responsibilities:

  • To achieve Sales, Gross Profit Margin and Net Margin targets as per the budget.
  • Ensure all staff members are trained to EIQA Standards where appropriate, and ensure the level of hygiene is of the highest standard throughout the store, and all staff members comply.
  • To ensure hygiene standards are to the highest standards, including a comprehensive HACCP Plan following EIQA and EHO.
  • Have in-depth knowledge of all Health & Safety regulations and how they relate to the store.
  • To ensure merchandising and presentation in the Fresh Departments are to the highest standards at all times.
  • Ensure weekly stocktaking procedures are adhered to.
  • To attend weekly management meetings and hold Fresh Departmental Meetings subsequently to ensure accurate communication of departmental performance and goal setting.
  • To ensure the smooth running of Food Production Operations.
  • To ensure costings on all In-house produced products are accurate and updated.
  • To handle customer requests, queries and complaints following company procedures
  • To draw up and control staff rosters, ensuring adequate cover within budgeted hours.
  • To develop new concepts and ideas and ensure successful implementation.
  • Ensure company rules, policies and procedures are adhered to at all times.
  • To ensure the highest standards of Customer Service are given to all customers at all times.
  • To assume store manager responsibilities in their absence.
  • To conduct any other duties as directed
  • To seek opportunities to develop yourself in technical training and professional development.
  • To implement a comprehensive succession plan with talent identified, coached and developed with appropriate training provided.

Qualifications and Experience

  • IT Literate with excellent communication skills.
  • People skills with the ability to lead and motivate a team.
  • The ability to work in high-pressure situations.
  • Ability to read and understand sales data.
  • Excellent organisational and time management skills.
  • Self-motivated and enthusiastic with a high level of confidence.
  • A strong work ethic.
  • Ability to display professionalism and reliability.
  • Previous retail Managerial experience is required.

This role is an excellent opportunity for anyone looking to advance their career in an exciting company. Competitive salary with exceptional opportunities for training & promotion within the Retail Group

job.title: Oncology Inpatient Nurse
job.description:
Key Responsibilities and Deliverable

  • Direct Patient Care:
    • Deliver direct care to assigned patients.
    • Conduct nursing history, summarize data, and identify nursing diagnoses and patient care needs.
    • Observe and record patient signs, symptoms, behaviors, and physiological status; communicate assessments and propose care revisions.
    • Implement individualized care plans for newly admitted patients as per policy.
    • Administer nursing interventions consistent with the medical care plan.
    • Handle admission, discharge, and transfer procedures; assist with patient activities and care.
    • Execute physician orders; safely administer medications and treatments.
    • Notify nursing and medical staff of any changes in patient status.
    • Independently assume responsibility for assigned patient care.
    • Perform specialty service techniques and routines.
    • Maintain aseptic techniques, isolation procedures, and infection control measures.
    • Document all nursing care in patient records.
    • Ensure patient privacy and confidentiality at all times.
    • Evaluate and reassess patient care, revising interventions and outcomes as necessary.
    • Assess patient understanding and compliance with healthcare instructions.
    • Review teaching documentation with the Nurse Manager or designee.
    • Adhere to department internal controls.

Clinical Responsibilities

  • Adhere to The Professional Scope of Practice Framework 2000 (Nursing & Midwife Board of Ireland).
  • Ensure individual patient assessments, care plans, and evaluations are in place.
  • Involve patients’ families and significant others as appropriate.
  • Provide care in optimal clinical environments, following all nursing and hospital policies.
  • Participate in and supervise patient meals and dietary needs.
  • Adhere to visiting time policies.
  • Delegate tasks appropriately based on skill level and knowledge.
  • Record documentation professionally, legibly, and promptly.

Managerial Responsibilities

  • Identify and communicate issues to the Nurse Manager promptly.
  • Demonstrate confidence and competence in hospital policies and guidelines.
  • Efficiently record necessary documentation.
  • Manage complaints effectively.
  • Monitor risk management processes.
  • Maintain effective interdisciplinary communication.
  • Deputize for the Nurse Manager as needed.
  • Engage in ward and hospital nursing communication.

Personal and Professional Responsibilities

  • Maintain a professional portfolio.
  • Utilize opportunities to educate patients and their families.
  • Attend relevant study days and courses.
  • Act as a preceptor or supervisor to students and new staff.
  • Participate in performance reviews with the Nurse Manager.

Educational Responsibilities

  • Enhance learning opportunities in the clinical area.
  • Participate in the clinical induction of new nursing and support staff.
  • Take responsibility for personal learning and development needs.

Qualifications

  • Registered General Nurse license in good standing with the Nursing & Midwife Board of Ireland (NMBI).

Experience

  • Preferably, 1 year of post-nursing registration experience.
  • Oncology experience is preferred.

Job-Specific Competencies and Knowledge

  • Teamwork: Ability to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and demonstrate motivation and innovation.
  • Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Effective communication, presenting information clearly and concisely, and understanding change management.
  • Planning and Organising: Evidence of effective planning, organizing, and time management skills; flexibility in rotations, rostering, and attitude to work.
  • Knowledge: Recent and relevant experience in the specialized area and acute hospital setting; knowledge of new developments in specialized areas and national strategies in nursing care.
  • Patient Focus: Commitment to quality care, empathy, and treating patients, relatives, and colleagues with dignity and respect.

INDFRS1

job.title: Senior Lettings Agent
job.description:
Senior Lettings Agent required for a Dublin-based property developer and operator with more than 20 years of collective property sector experience. The business works across the full lifecycle of an asset, from development and deal management through to letting, property management and financial reporting.

The Role

As Senior Lettings Negotiator, you will play a key role in the lease-up of new residential developments while managing day-to-day lettings activity across an established portfolio. You will work closely with residents, clients, accounts, maintenance and property management colleagues to maintain high occupancy levels and deliver an excellent resident experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the full residential lettings cycle, from enquiry through to move-in.
  • Lead lease-up activity for new residential developments.
  • Conduct property tours, present apartments and negotiate rents.
  • Manage tenant selection, referencing, onboarding and lease execution.
  • Manage re-lets and ensure vacant units are returned to market efficiently.
  • Carry out rent reviews in line with current legislation.
  • Manage licence renewals and statutory compliance requirements.
  • Conduct property inspections and condition reporting.
  • Maintain strong relationships with residents, clients and landlords.
  • Work closely with accounts, maintenance and property management teams.
  • Provide regular client reporting and portfolio updates.
  • Build relationships with relevant organisations, including technology and finance companies and third-level institutions.
  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of landlord and tenant legislation.

Who are you

  • Previous experience in residential lettings, property management or a closely related property role.
  • PSRA Category C Licence.
  • Strong knowledge of the Residential Tenancies Act.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and relationship-building skills.
  • Commercially minded, proactive and solution-focused.
  • Strong organisation, attention to detail and time management.
  • Confident managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Full clean driving licence and access to a car.

Whats on offer

  • €40,000–€55,000 salary
  • Career development within a growing property business
  • Exposure to a substantial residential portfolio and new developments
  • Collaborative and supportive working environment

Aurora Enriching Lives, Enriching Communities

Person In Charge – Permanent Contract – Full Time

“Do you have the vision & passion to be a key driver and champion of supporting people to live determined lives”

Aurora provides residential and day services for adults with Intellectual Disabilities in a community-based setting with supports. Aurora has a highly trained and dedicated staff of more than 300 health-care professionals catering to the needs of over 80 adults with Intellectual Disabilities.

We are looking for candidates to be a key driver and champion of supporting people to live self-determined lives and to be a central communicator with all stakeholders including families, multi-disciplinary teams, psychologist, senior management, community, employers and others. The PIC will lead the house on a day-to-day basis and in consultation with their line manager when key decisions are being made. He/she should be flexible in their approach to service provision and have the ability to work as a team member. He/she will be required to take an active part in ensuring that day-to-day operations of the Services reflect the ethos and vision of Aurora and the needs of the people supported are being met through professional work practices.

Qualifications Required

  • A relevant Management qualification is essential.
  • Registration with CORU (where applicable)

Essential

  • Full clean driving licence and own transportation (Manual)

Essential skills and experience:

  • 3 Years managerial experience in a health care role.
  • Proven practical experience or similar experience in a role of this level.
  • Proven knowledge and experience of HIQA standards and Certification.
  • Passion for innovative solutions and process improvement
  • Excellent analytical skills
  • Proven organisational and time management skills
  • Evidence of effective resource planning
  • The ability to lead the team by example, coaching and supporting individuals
  • Strong interpersonal and networking skills including strong written communication skills

Benefits of working with us:

Competitive salary linked to HSE Social Care Leader (depending on skills & experience) €57484 - €67130

  • Training Opportunities

  • Fortnightly pay

job.title: Senior Speech and Language Therapist - Hybrid 4 Day week
job.description:
Senior Speech and Language Therapist (Paediatric)

Location: Co. Wicklow (Hybrid)
Hours: 32 hours per week (flexible hybrid working)
Contract: Permanent
Reports to: Clinical Lead / Director
Salary: Negotiable - depending on experience

About the Service

We are working with a growing multidisciplinary children’s service providing high-quality, evidence-based assessment and intervention to children and young people.

The team works closely with families, schools and other healthcare professionals to ensure a holistic, child-centred approach to care.

The service has a strong emphasis on professional autonomy, collaboration and maintaining a healthy work-life balance while delivering high clinical standards.

The Role

We are seeking an enthusiastic and compassionate Speech and Language Therapist to join a supportive multidisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will assess and support children presenting with a range of communication needs and will work closely alongside Occupational Therapists, Psychologists and Assistant Psychologists.

This role offers flexibility, autonomy and the opportunity to contribute to the ongoing development of a growing private paediatric service.

Key Responsibilities

  • Carry out comprehensive Speech and Language assessments
  • Develop individualised therapy programmes
  • Deliver evidence-based intervention
  • Assess speech, language, communication and social communication needs
  • Work with children with developmental language disorder, speech sound disorders, autism, ADHD and other neurodevelopmental presentations
  • Complete feeding and swallowing assessments where appropriately trained
  • Provide AAC recommendations where appropriate
  • Produce high-quality assessment and therapy reports
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation
  • Liaise with parents, schools, preschools and other professionals
  • Participate in multidisciplinary assessments and team meetings
  • Contribute to integrated reports and case discussions
  • Support service development and quality improvement initiatives

Flexible Hybrid Working

This role offers a flexible hybrid working model to support both clinical delivery and work-life balance.

Working hours can be scheduled between 7am and 7pm Monday to Friday, subject to service needs.

Clinicians may select preferred working days in advance (minimum two weeks’ notice required to support scheduling).

Report writing, admin tasks, intake calls and preparation work can be completed remotely where appropriate.

A minimum of one on-site clinic day per week is required, with additional attendance for assessments, MDT clinics, parent meetings and service needs.

Essential Criteria

  • Qualification in Speech and Language Therapy
  • Experience working in Paediatric assessments ideally 3 years we would consider someone with 18+ months exp solely in paediatrics.
  • CORU registration
  • Experience working with a paediatric caseload
  • Strong communication skills
  • Ability to work independently and within a multidisciplinary team
  • Good organisation and time management skills
  • Full driving licence and access to transport

Desirable Experience

Experience in any of the following areas would be an advantage:

  • Autism
  • ADHD
  • Developmental Language Disorder
  • Speech Sound Disorders
  • Social Communication Difficulties
  • Early Intervention
  • School-aged populations
  • AAC
  • Parent coaching
  • School-based consultation

Benefits

  • Flexible hybrid working model
  • Monthly clinical supervision
  • CPD contribution
  • Private health insurance contribution
  • Fuel allowance for approved travel
  • Company mobile phone and laptop provided
  • Administrative support
  • Protected report writing time
  • 25 days annual leave (pro rata)
  • 7 days certified sick pay per year (policy dependent)
  • Maternity support scheme after qualifying service
  • Opportunity to contribute to service development within a growing team
  • Future leadership potential as the service expands

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for someone who is:

  • Child-centred in their approach
  • Confident working independently
  • Collaborative within a team setting
  • Strong in clinical reasoning
  • Passionate about evidence-based practice
  • Committed to continuous learning and development
  • Comfortable working in a growing and evolving service

job.title: Social Worker - Team Lead
job.description:
Social Work Team Leader – Duty Child Protection

Location: North Dublin / Ballymun area
Contract: Permanent, Full-Time
Hours: 35 hours per week
Salary: €68,217 – €78,687 per annum
Service: Duty Child Protection (DCP)

FRS Recruitment is working with a leading statutory Child and Family Agency to recruit an experienced Social Work Team Leader to join their Duty Child Protection service in North Dublin.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Social Worker who is ready to take the next step in their career and take on a leadership position within a statutory child protection service.

The successful candidate will join an established Duty Child Protection team, providing professional leadership and support within a service focused on the safety, welfare and wellbeing of children and families.

About the Role

The Social Work Team Leader will play a key role in supporting the delivery of an effective, responsive and high-quality Duty Child Protection service.

Working within a child-centred and family-focused environment, you will provide professional leadership and guidance to Social Work staff, supporting effective decision-making and high standards of practice.

The role will suit an experienced Social Worker who has a strong understanding of child protection and safeguarding and is looking to develop their leadership career within a statutory setting.

You will have the opportunity to use your professional expertise while supporting colleagues in managing complex situations and contributing to positive outcomes for children and families.

Key Responsibilities

As Social Work Team Leader, your responsibilities will include:

  • Providing professional leadership, guidance and support to Social Work staff within the Duty Child Protection service.
  • Supporting Social Workers with professional decision-making and the management of complex child protection and welfare matters.
  • Promoting high standards of social work practice and ensuring a child-centred approach to service delivery.
  • Supporting effective assessment, risk management and case planning.
  • Providing advice and professional guidance to team members where required.
  • Supporting the effective management and allocation of work within the service.
  • Promoting good communication and collaborative working across the wider service.
  • Working effectively with colleagues and relevant external agencies involved in supporting children and families.
  • Contributing to service development, quality improvement and the ongoing development of professional practice.
  • Promoting a culture of reflective practice, learning and continuous professional development.
  • Supporting the delivery of a safe, effective and responsive child protection service.
  • Ensuring professional practice is carried out in line with relevant legislation, policies, procedures and professional standards.
  • Travel may be required as part of the role, therefore access to transport is desirable.

About You

We are looking for an experienced Social Work professional with a strong background in child protection and a genuine commitment to improving outcomes for children and families.

You will ideally have experience working within a statutory or child protection environment and be confident providing professional guidance and support to colleagues.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Significant experience working as a Social Worker.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of child protection and safeguarding practice.
  • The ability to provide professional leadership and guidance to Social Work colleagues.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent organisational and case management abilities.
  • The ability to assess situations, manage risk and make sound professional decisions.
  • Confidence working with complex and sensitive cases.
  • The ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary and multi-agency environment.
  • A commitment to high-quality, child-centred social work practice.
  • Strong resilience and the ability to work effectively within a demanding service environment.
  • A proactive approach to professional development and continuous improvement.
  • Access to transport is desirable due to the requirements of the role.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced Social Worker to progress into a Team Leader position within a national statutory Child and Family service.

The role offers the opportunity to take on greater professional responsibility while continuing to make a meaningful contribution to the safety and wellbeing of children and families.

The role offers:

  • Permanent, full-time employment.
  • 35-hour working week.
  • Salary of €68,217 – €78,687 per annum.
  • A leadership opportunity within a well-established statutory service.
  • The opportunity to develop your leadership and professional experience.
  • The opportunity to contribute to the delivery and development of Duty Child Protection services.
  • A meaningful role with significant responsibility and impact.

How to Apply

If you are an experienced Social Worker with a background in Child Protection and are ready to take the next step in your career, we would be delighted to hear from you.

For more information or a confidential discussion about this opportunity, please contact Julie O Sullivan at

job.title: Assistant Purchasing Manager- Cork
job.description:
My client, a leading Industrial Supplies Distributor based on the outskirts of Cork City, is seeking an Assistant Purchasing Manager to join their team.

Working within the senior management team and overseeing a team of Buyers, you will be responsible for overseeing the category Procurement budget, implementing and streamlining processes, sourcing new suppliers and any other duties as required for the department. This is a fantastic opportunity for an Assistant Purchasing Manager to grow on their career in a thriving organization.

This would suit a candidate who has a background in Construction, Industrial Manufacturing or Plumbing and has a proven track record of success in Procurement.

The responsibilities for the Assistant Purchasing Manager include but are not limited to:

  • Support the head-of-department by assisting in the development and implementation of Procurement Strategy, aligned to the overall Category Strategy
  • Monitor market dynamics, industry developments, competitive landscape, emerging technologies, to identify opportunities, inform procurement decisions, mitigate risks.
  • Manage product ranges within the portfolio, a competitive & innovative assortment.
  • Manage internal procurement processes (sales history, forecasting demand, purchase requisitions, stock purchase orders, stock transfers) as well as supply-chain considerations (capacity, constraints, lead times, delivery schedules) - to ensure material requirements are met ‘on time & in full’.
  • Optimise inventory levels to minimize stockouts and excess inventory.
  • Negotiate terms & conditions, price, request for proposals (RFP’s), request for quotation (RFQ’s), bid evaluations, delivery charge - to ensure optimal product cost.
  • Leverage market insight, understand competitiveness (price index), take on board sales team feedback, implement price management strategies to maximise profitability and competitiveness & optimise margin.
  • Utilise data-driven insights to track portfolio performance against target (sales, cost, margin, service, stock) and drive continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate with suppliers, build relationships. Drive availability, innovation, lowest cost & drive continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate with suppliers, build relationships to deliver customer-centric initiatives and drive profitable growth.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to understand requirements of the procurement function & drive portfolio success.

The qualifications for the desired Assistant Purchasing Manager include:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Business or related field
  • Strong commercial acumen, with proven experience at Senior Purchasing Management level (+3 years),
  • preferably within wholesale or retail industries, preferably in the Irish market.
  • Solid analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex data and market trends, translate into insight to facilitate informed commercial decisions.
  • Strong communication, engagement & presentation skills. Ability to engage stakeholders & influence positive outcomes.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, particularly Excel, and experience with purchasing platforms and ERP systems.
  • Excellent organisational and time management skills
  • Strong leadership skills with proven people management experience.
  • Work as part of team to enhance production performance and minimise risks.
  • Attention to detail in completing tasks in a proficient and timely manner.
  • Hardworking and reliable

If you feel that you fulfil the above requirements please apply today with your CV. If you have any further queries please contact Rachael Pando of FRS Recruitment

  • Virtual Ward Services

  • Support the implementation of HSE and organisational service developments.

Leadership & Team Support

  • Act as a point of escalation in the absence of the Operations Manager.
  • Promote a positive, collaborative and patient-centred culture.
  • Support staff development, training and performance management processes.

Out-of-Hours Responsibilities

Essential Requirements

  • Minimum 5 years post Nursing Qualification
  • Strong understanding of healthcare governance, quality and compliance requirements.
  • Excellent organisational, communication and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience working with multidisciplinary teams and external stakeholders.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and healthcare management systems.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience supporting operational delivery across multiple healthcare services.
  • Knowledge of HSE-funded community healthcare programmes.
  • Experience participating in an on-call management rota.

  • Opportunity to work across a diverse range of innovative healthcare services.
  • Supportive leadership team and collaborative working environment.
  • Professional development and career progression opportunities.
  • Access to training, mentoring and leadership development programmes.
  • Hybrid working across office, community and service locations.
  • Participation in strategic service development and organisational growth initiatives.

HR Compliance Advisor

Location: Co. Cavan

Permanent Full Time

Hybrid Working - 2 days remote

Salary: €45,000 plus 10% bonus, private company pension and increasing annual leave with service.

The purpose of this role is to ensure the organisation consistently meets its obligations under Irish employment legislation, regulatory standards, and internal HR policies. The HR Compliance Officer will manage and monitor compliance activities relating to work authorisation, right-to-work verification, working time regulations, people data governance, and other key HR compliance areas, supporting effective risk management and maintaining a state of ongoing audit readiness.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage all aspects of work permit and immigration compliance, including applications, renewals, tracking, and expiry monitoring.
  • Liaise with external stakeholders, including government bodies, legal advisors, and relocation providers.
  • Ensure robust right-to-work verification processes and maintain compliance with employment eligibility requirements.
  • Support internal and external audits relating to immigration and work authorisation.
  • Monitor compliance with the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997, including working hours, rest periods, breaks, night work, and Sunday working requirements.
  • Partner with Operations, Payroll, and HR to review attendance data and identify compliance risks.
  • Support corrective actions and maintain accurate records to demonstrate statutory compliance.
  • Support GDPR compliance across HR processes, including data retention, lawful processing, access controls, and data minimisation.
  • Act as a key HR contact for data protection audits, DSARs, and people data governance matters.
  • Promote best practices in the management and protection of employee data.
  • Maintain accurate, audit-ready HR records and documentation in line with legal and organisational requirements.
  • Support internal compliance reviews and external audits, including WRC, customer, and certification audits.
  • Identify compliance gaps and drive corrective actions to completion.
  • Support the review, implementation, and monitoring of HR policies, procedures, and SOPs.
  • Maintain documentation and evidence to demonstrate compliance across HR activities.
  • Ensure all compliance requirements are completed during onboarding, including contracts, right-to-work checks, and employment permits.
  • Monitor compliance throughout the employee lifecycle, including recruitment, transfers, role changes, and offboarding.
  • Partner with Recruitment, Payroll, and HR Operations to ensure consistent and compliant processes.
  • Conduct periodic audits of employee records and lifecycle activities.
  • Support continuous improvement of onboarding and employee lifecycle compliance processes.
  • Monitor and report on key HR compliance metrics, including work permits, working time compliance, and audit findings.
  • Identify emerging compliance risks and legislative changes, recommending actions to mitigate exposure.
  • Support the Head of People & Development in managing people-related risk and maintaining audit readiness.
  • Maintain compliance reporting and tracking mechanisms to monitor performance and risk.
  • Drive continuous improvement of HR compliance processes, systems, controls, and documentation.
  • Promote a culture of compliance through stakeholder engagement, communication, and best-practice governance.

Skills & Qualifications:

  • 3+ years’ experience in HR operations, HR compliance, or workforce compliance roles.
  • Strong hands‑on experience with Irish work permits / immigration processes.
  • Working knowledge of Irish employment law, particularly working time legislation.
  • Experience in manufacturing, production, FMCG or similar sector.
  • Relevant third‑level qualification in HR or related discipline.
  • CIPD qualification (or working towards) desirable.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and compliance discipline.
  • Strong understanding of Irish employment legislation and HR regulatory frameworks.
  • Ability to interpret legislation and translate it into practical HR controls.
  • Strong organisational and record‑keeping skills.
  • Confident communicator with the ability to challenge non‑compliance constructively.
  • Proactive, risk‑aware and solutions‑focused mindset.

job.title: Senior Project Manager
job.description:
Senior Project Manager

Location: Dunboyne, Co. Meath (Hybrid Working Model)

Introduction

A leading provider of communications, SCADA and instrumentation solutions, working across industrial sectors including water, power, utilities, corporate business, broadcasting and public safety. With a proven track record spanning over four decades, the organisation delivers innovative infrastructure and technology solutions to a diverse client base.

Overview of Role

As Senior Project Manager, you will be responsible for the successful delivery of significant multi-site infrastructure programmes. Acting as the primary interface between the company, clients, engineering consultancies and the wider supply chain, you will ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within scope and to agreed commercial objectives.

This is not a purely administrative project management position. We are looking for a commercially astute and delivery-focused professional who can independently lead major projects, manage contractual relationships, identify and secure project variations, control budgets and represent the company confidently at senior stakeholder level.

While experience in SCADA, automation or Operational Technology (OT) is advantageous, we are equally interested in candidates with strong commercial project management experience gained within infrastructure, engineering, utilities or similarly complex technical environments.

The Candidate

You are a commercially aware and delivery-driven project professional who takes ownership and leads from the front. You proactively manage programmes, identify risks and commercial opportunities, challenge assumptions and ensure accountability across project teams.

You are equally comfortable engaging with senior client stakeholders and engineering teams and can confidently lead complex project discussions while maintaining a strong focus on delivery, commercial performance and customer satisfaction.

Responsibilities

Project Leadership & Delivery

  • Take full day-to-day ownership of a major multi-site infrastructure project from mobilisation through to commissioning, handover and contractual closeout.
  • Develop, own and maintain the detailed project delivery programme, including design, procurement, engineering, FAT, site deployment, SAT and commissioning activities.
  • Maintain a clear understanding of the critical path and proactively manage project dependencies, constraints, interfaces and recovery actions.
  • Lead project mobilisation, kick-off meetings, internal delivery reviews, client progress meetings and programme reviews.
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary engineering resources, subcontractors, suppliers and external partners to achieve agreed milestones.
  • Ensure project deliverables are clearly defined, allocated, tracked and driven to completion.
  • Provide concise, accurate and timely project reporting to the Head of Delivery & Service and senior management.

Commercial & Financial Management

  • Take a commercially proactive approach to project delivery and actively protect the company's contractual and financial position.
  • Understand the project scope, pricing assumptions, commercial structure, contract requirements and agreed exclusions in detail.
  • Manage project budgets, cost forecasts, revenue, cashflow and cost-to-complete in conjunction with Finance and Commercial teams.
  • Prepare and support monthly applications for payment, ensuring completed work and earned value are accurately reflected in project valuations.
  • Identify scope change, additional works and potential variations at the earliest possible opportunity and ensure they are formally recorded.
  • Ensure variations are commercially assessed, priced and agreed before additional work is undertaken wherever practicable.
  • Monitor project margin and forecast financial performance throughout the project lifecycle, implementing corrective action where required.
  • Challenge scope creep and ensure the company is appropriately compensated for work outside the agreed contractual scope.
  • Maintain robust commercial records, project correspondence and supporting documentation for all claims, changes and decisions.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

  • Act as the primary day-to-day project contact for the client and associated engineering consultancy organisations.
  • Develop strong working relationships with client project teams, engineering consultants, operational stakeholders and third-party suppliers.
  • Lead structured client progress meetings and provide clear updates on programme, risk, commercial matters, actions and project delivery.
  • Manage stakeholder expectations through proactive communication, formal reporting and timely escalation of issues.
  • Represent the company professionally and confidently in senior project, technical and commercial discussions.
  • Work collaboratively with major engineering consultancy groups while ensuring the company's delivery and commercial interests remain appropriately represented.

Engineering & Technical Coordination

  • Work closely with Principal Engineers and technical specialists to coordinate design and engineering activities.
  • Ensure technical deliverables, Functional Design Specifications, drawings and engineering documentation are developed in line with the approved programme.
  • Coordinate technical reviews, FAT, SAT and commissioning activities and ensure actions are driven to timely closure.
  • Ensure engineering resources have clearly defined priorities, deliverables and deadlines.
  • Facilitate resolution of technical issues and ensure the appropriate engineering expertise is engaged where required.
  • Maintain sufficient technical understanding to lead complex systems integration projects; detailed hands-on SCADA programming experience is not essential.

Essential Experience

Technical & Professional

  • Minimum 5 years' project management experience within infrastructure, engineering, utilities, systems integration or a similarly complex technical environment.
  • Demonstrable experience delivering projects or programmes with values typically in excess of €1 million.
  • Proven experience managing complex, multi-site or phased delivery programmes from mobilisation through to handover.

job.title: Contract Fencing Manager - Wicklow
job.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

JOB TITLE: Contract Fencing Manager

ROLE TYPE: Permanent Full-Time

LOCATION: Hybrid – Field & office based (Tinahely, Co. Wicklow)

REPORTING TO: Regional Fencing Manager

About FRS Co-Op

FRS Co-Op was founded in 1980 by farmers to support their communities, and as Ireland has grown, so have we. Today we’re a multi-sector co-op with a focus on innovation, made up of fair minded experts who live and work in the communities that we serve. The FRS Co-Op has been finding ways to make Ireland work better for everyone for almost fifty years. While we still have farming in our DNA, it’s only part of what we do.

FRS Fencing is a division of FRS Co-Op, a trusted provider of premium fencing solutions across Ireland. We serve a wide network of resellers and retailers, combining decades of industry expertise with a commitment to quality, innovation, and customer partnership. Our mission is to support the growth and success of our customers through best-in-class fencing products and installation services.

Purpose of Role

The FRS Fencing - Contract Fencing Manager is responsible for driving sales of premium fencing products and installation services to members and customers of our cooperative. This role will focus on expanding market share, building strong relationships with key accounts, and identifying new business opportunities to support the continued growth of FRS Fencing.

Main Responsibilities & Activities

  • Proactively identify, target, and acquire new customers across Ireland.
  • Manage and grow relationships with existing customers, ensuring high levels of satisfaction and repeat business.
  • Develop and execute a strategic sales plan to achieve ambitious growth targets.
  • Conduct regular market analysis to identify trends, competitor activity, and new opportunities.
  • Represent FRS Fencing at industry events, trade shows, and customer meetings.
  • Collaborate with internal teams (central purchasing, marketing) to ensure seamless order fulfilment and customer support.
  • Prepare and deliver compelling sales presentations, proposals, and quotations.
  • Negotiate pricing, terms, and contracts in line with company guidelines.
  • Gather customer feedback and market intelligence to inform product development and service improvements.
  • Maintain accurate records of sales activity, pipeline, and customer interactions using sales tracking tools.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • New business acquisition and onboarding of fencing accounts.
  • Growth in sales revenue, margin and market share within our contract fencing business.
  • Achievement of monthly and annual sales targets.
  • Customer retention and satisfaction scores.
  • Quality and accuracy of sales invoicing (CRM/ERP), tracking and reporting.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Experience: Proven track record in sales, preferably in agriculture, building materials, construction, or related sectors.
  • Education: Degree in Business, Sales, Marketing, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • Full clean driving license and willingness to travel extensively.

Key Skills & Competencies

  • Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills; able to present and negotiate at all levels.
  • Relationship Building: Strong ability to develop and maintain long-term partnerships with customers.
  • Commercial Acumen: Results-driven with a strong understanding of sales processes and market dynamics.
  • Problem-Solving: Resourceful and proactive in addressing challenges and seizing opportunities.
  • Product Knowledge: Willingness to learn and promote the technical features and benefits of FRS Fencing products.
  • Collaboration: Team player who works effectively with colleagues across departments.
  • Tech-Savvy: Proficient in CRM & billing systems, Microsoft Office, and digital communication tools.
  • Customer-Centric Mindset: Passionate about delivering outstanding service and value to customers.#

Apply today by sending forward your updated CV or contacting Gerry Farrell at FRS Recruitment

job.title: SCADA Engineer
job.description:
SCADA Engineer
Location: Dunboyne, Co. Meath (Hybrid)

We're seeking a motivated SCADA Engineer to join our growing team. Ideal for an Electrical, Automation, Computer or SCADA Engineer with strong technical skills, sharp problem-solving ability, and an eye for system design. You'll gain exposure to SCADA, telemetry, PLC integration and instrumentation technologies, playing a key role across the design, configuration, testing, deployment and support of SCADA solutions. Automation experience — particularly with Bristol Babcock PLCs — is a plus.

This is a predominantly office-based role with occasional site visits for deployment, commissioning and support. You'll work primarily with SCADA platforms Ignition and ICONICS, supporting integration with PLCs, RTUs, telemetry outstations and client systems, while maintaining regular client communication and troubleshooting support. We're looking for someone innovative, willing to challenge existing processes and drive continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support pre-sales and design of new SCADA solutions
  • Respond to client requests, incidents and support events
  • Collaborate on implementation, testing and support of HMI, SCADA, PLC and telemetry software
  • Produce design specs, configuration documentation and project records
  • Configure, develop, test and support applications on Ignition and ICONICS
  • Deliver post-implementation client training
  • Manage project files, licensing and documentation
  • Liaise with client IT on security and system requirements
  • Build reusable libraries to improve delivery efficiency
  • Contribute to estimates, work breakdown structures and delivery plans

Essential Requirements

  • Strong grasp of SCADA architecture and components
  • Experience with Ignition and/or ICONICS
  • Cloud experience (Azure, AWS or similar)
  • Knowledge of Modbus, DNP3, OPC and other SCADA protocols
  • Experience with telemetry, HMI configuration and industrial communications
  • Ability to interpret PLC/RTU/telemetry interfaces
  • Microsoft SQL database knowledge
  • Familiarity with remote support tools (RDP, TeamViewer)
  • Understanding of Ethernet/TCP/IP networking
  • Awareness of industrial cybersecurity practices
  • SCADA alarm/notification design experience
  • Full Irish driving licence, with flexibility to travel

Desirable

  • PLC programming, especially Bristol Babcock
  • AI, data science or statistical analysis experience
  • VB/SQL development skills

Only candidates based in Ireland with full right to work will be considered.

  • Proficiency in relevant engineering software, such as Autodesk Inventor, Altium or Python, depending on discipline.
  • Knowledge of part design, product design, assemblies, engineering drawings and design for manufacture.
  • Strong understanding of engineering design principles and methodologies.
  • An interest in practical product development, particularly products used within agricultural, mechanical or outdoor working environments, would be an advantage.
  • Experience with machine design or automation would be beneficial but is not essential.
  • Experience preparing technical documentation, manuals, specifications or project plans would also be an advantage.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a successful, growing business and gain hands-on experience across the complete product development process.

Apply now or contact Kerry Rickard for a confidential discussion.
